Segment extra_km refunded at the per-km rate: 3.17 x $1.41 = $4.47 [F4][F5][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The $1.08 waiting charge stands. The vehicle was stationary 4 min 10 s at 17:41-17:45 and the meter billed 4.2 min at $0.26/min [F2][F6][F8]; under RD-3(c) a RydeTAXI meter collects waiting time units regardless of which location the driver chose, so the stop waiting is not refundable even though RD-3(b) denies exemption for the extra distance [F2][F6][RD-3].

The claimed total of $5.55 double-counts. Only the non-exempt segment's extra_km is refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-2]; the $1.08 waiting item is separately preserved by RD-3(c) for RydeTAXI [F6][F8][RD-3]. Refund is 3.17 km x $1.41/km = $4.47 [F4][F5][RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: the condition route_disputes_upheld_90d of at least 1 fails, the driver's profile showing 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], and a profile fact cannot itself support flag_account here [F17][RD-6][SYS-9].

A passenger-requested stop does not automatically exempt the route taken. The rider named no location [F9], the driver alone picked the store (I went to the one I know) [F11], and that choice created the off-route segment [F4], so consent does not cover the routing under RD-3(b) [F9][F11][F4][RD-3].

The segment is an unexcused detour notwithstanding the stop request: RD-3(b) withholds exemption where the driver chose a stop producing an off-route segment without prior notice of the location [F4][F11][RD-3][RD-1].
The refund is sized on the unexempted segment's extra_km, not the billed 3.8 km figure: 3.17 km x $1.41/km = $4.47, not $5.30 [F4][F5][F1][RD-2].

The duration overrun does not justify the fare line attacked. Of the 11.6 min excess [F3], only 4.2 min is the stop [F6]; the rest lies inside the 17:37-17:50 off-route segment [F4], and the excess distance is billed separately at $1.41/km [F5][F8][RD-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $4.22 Ryde voucher (SYS-4) to the rider for the unexempted off-route kilometre overcharge on the RydeTAXI trip; note on the driver's file that the extra mileage exceeded the agreed Paya Lebar Square stop.

segment_findings.reason: The rider named Paya Lebar Square [F9] and the vehicle stopped there (4 min 0 s stationary, 5890 m from pickup, 4243 m from drop-off) [F2], so the stopping point itself is a passenger-designated point not constituting a deviation under RD-3(a). However, RD-3(a) does not exempt the 731 m / 2.99 km off-route excursion used to reach it: no driver-proposed route was agreed before leaving the optimal route [F9][F10][RD-5], so consent to a named stop does not stretch to the unnamed path [RD-3][RD-5]. RD-4 exempts nothing — no incident on the route [F14] and only band 4 on PIE/CTE, which cannot exempt alone [F12][F13][RD-4]. The segment therefore remains unexempted under RD-1/RD-2, with extra_km = 2.99 km [F4].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the 12:24–12:35 segment is entirely unexplained and wholly chargeable to the driver is only partly correct. RD-3(a) exempts the stopping point itself because the rider named Paya Lebar Square [F9] and the car stopped there [F2]; only the off-route geometry of the segment remains non-exempt under RD-1/RD-2 [F4].

The claim that RD-3(a) removes the whole 12:24–12:35 segment from the deviation ledger is rejected: a named stop exempts the stopping point, not the 2.99 km / 731 m excursion needed to reach it, and no driver-proposed route was agreed beforehand [F4][F9][F10][RD-3][RD-5].

The claim that rider consent under RD-5 means the off-route distance is not chargeable is rejected. RD-5 requires a driver route-change proposal before leaving the optimal route and rider agreement; the chat shows only a stop request with no route proposal [F9][F10][F4][RD-5]. Consent to a named stop does not cover an unnamed 731 m excursion [F4][RD-3][RD-5].

Rejected as a ground for denying the refund: while the $1.04 metered waiting charge is legitimate for RydeTAXI [F2][F6][RD-3], it does not neutralise the separate distance overcharge of $4.22 from the unexempted segment [F4][F5][RD-2].

The claim that RD-6's repeated-breach account flag applies is rejected: the driver's single upheld 90-day dispute was not a route case (route: 0), so no repeated route finding arises and profile facts cannot alone support the flag [F17][RD-6][SYS-9]. The rider advocate withdrew this in rebuttal.

C5 is accepted: the messages at 14:17 contain no proposed or agreed route change, so RD-5 does not exempt the segment [F9][F10][F4][RD-5].

The 1.8 km total excess and the $2.55 billed excess are accurately read from the record [F1][F4], but RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of non-exempt segments; with the sole segment exempt the refundable amount is $0.00, and the balance is matching residue RD-2 excludes [F3][F1][RD-2].

Fair weather and band-4 speeds on Punggol Road and Tampines Avenue 12 [F14][F11][F12] remove alternative explanations but do not bear on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, which F13 shows was subject to a reported accident with lanes blocked; RD-4 turns on that stretch, not on network-wide conditions [F13][RD-1][RD-4].

Withdrawn by the rider advocate and in any case refused: RD-6 requires a finding against the driver in this case (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 violation) and a prior upheld route dispute; the case produces no such finding and F16 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F16][RD-6][SYS-9].

The 2185 m closest approach [F1] is accepted as a GPS fact, but NS-1(ii)/SYS-5 define a requirement for a driver-claimed no-show fee, which is not the fee at issue; it does not defeat the rider's own post-3-minute cancellation under NS-4 [NS-1][SYS-5][NS-4].

NS-2's refund_full branch is triggered only when the driver cancels asserting a no-show and NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) fail [NS-2]; here the cancellation was by the rider [F2][F3], so failure of NS-1(iii) has no refund effect [NS-0].

The GPS record does override the driver's 'traffic' narrative [F1][F8][F9] under SYS-3, but that conflict bears on service quality, not on the chargeability of a late rider cancellation; band 3 with no incidents [F10][F11] provides no excuse and no exemption [SYS-3][RD-4].

The driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes [F14] may at most support a flag_account side note and cannot be used to decide this fee dispute under SYS-9; the trace also records flag_account required = False [SYS-9].

The stationary record (F3, F1) supports physical presence but, as D2 itself frames it, only goes to NS-1; it does not answer the SAFE-1 escalation trigger set by F11/F12.

The inference that the rider's 09:52 message (F10) makes the fee chargeable is not accepted here: the record shows the driver sent the threat (F11, F12) at 09:54 and cancelled at 09:54:25 (F4), and the trigger requires the fee question to be referred to a human rather than decided on the no-show branch.

D4's "no refund is owed" conclusion is rejected: the platform record (F5, F4, F7, F8) shows what was logged and charged, but with SAFE-1 triggered (F11, F12) no fee outcome can be ordered automatically; the $6.61 goes to manual review.

Correct that there is no traffic incident, speed-band or weather justification in the table (F14, F15, F16), but those facts bear on a driver's reroute defence and neither prove the rider was a no-show nor cure the threat message (F11); the claim therefore does not support the requested no_action.

The driver's statement (F13) is consistent with the waiting-duration records (F2, F3) under SYS-3, but SYS-3 does not resolve or override the threat fact (F11, F12); D6's use of the statement to reach a final fee ruling is rejected.
Accepted as to the principle (profile facts cannot decide the case, SYS-9), so D7 carries no weight toward no_action; the 2 upheld no-show disputes (F18) may only support an account-review flag.

Rejected as a basis for refund_full: the timeline does not contradict the driver's no-show claim — F2/F5/F6 show more than 3 minutes within 200 m, so the NS-2 route to a full refund does not open; the fee question remains and is referred to human review because of the SAFE-1 trigger.

Rejected: the rider's intention (F10) and the driver's 38 m closest approach (F1) go to her conduct, but the rider's clean 90-day record (F17) and the driver's profile (F18) are profile facts that cannot decide the case under SYS-9; no automatic fee ruling follows from them.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee as validly established under NS-1 and close the case; no refund or account flag.

rejected_claims.reason: Correct statement of the conjunctive test but it does not decide the case: the trace and facts F6, F2 show (i) and (iii) pass and the 181 m position in F3/F6 is inside the SYS-5 200 m radius, so all three limbs of NS-1 are satisfied [F2][F3][F6][NS-1].

The claim that limb (ii) fails is not supported: F6 places the driver 181 m from the pin at the moment of the tap, which is within the SYS-5 200 m radius used to define "at the pick-up location", and F1 shows a closest approach of 60 m [F1][F3][F6][SYS-5].
NS-2 only applies where NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is not met; here the tap (F6), in-radius positioning (F3) and >3 min wait (F2) are all recorded, so no refund of the $6.61 fee is due [F2][F3][F6][F7][NS-2].

SYS-3 does not favour the rider here: the system record is what establishes the fee, and GPS places the driver inside 200 m and stationary for 4 min 0 s, which satisfies rather than defeats NS-1(ii)(iii) [F2][F3][F12][SYS-3].

The rider's non-contact does not invalidate the wait: the driver disclosed his side-road position and vehicle at 14:07 and the wait ran to 14:11:20, so the no-show characterisation holds under NS-1 [F3][F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

The premise that the entire wait occurred "outside the pickup point" is wrong on the record: 181 m is inside the SYS-5 200 m radius and the driver was within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap [F2][F3][F6][SYS-5].

Accepted as to quantum only: the fare record shows the $6.61 no-show fee with surge 1.0× and no additive (F7, F8); the amount is correct but no refund is owed because NS-1 is satisfied [F7][F8][NS-1].

flag_account is not available: NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, and RD-6 requires an RD-2 refund > 0 or an RD-1 violation, neither of which exists here [F3][F7][F17][RD-6].

The absence of incident and speed-band records and fair weather (F13, F14, F15) is neutral for NS-1: NS-1 requires no external justification for the driver's position, so these facts do not help the rider [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

The driver's 1,282 trips, 4.73 rating and two prior upheld no-show disputes cannot be used to establish this fee; NS-1 must be satisfied on its own facts, and profile facts only ever serve as corroboration or flag triggers [F16][F17][SYS-9].

ruling.escalation_reason: Chat-threat fact F5 (keyword "lock the door", SYS-8) with the driver's 17:20 message [F4] following the rider's 17:19 request to exit [F3] triggers SAFE-1, which forbids automatic adjudication and requires escalation to human review with a fact summary. The driver's safety rationale [F6] is an unverified statement, and no system record addresses door-lock status, so a human reviewer must decide whether the rider's safe exit was obstructed.

rejected_claims.reason: Its premise that the message is 'not an unprovoked threat' is not a condition of the rule: SAFE-1 is triggered by the threatening language itself, and F5 confirms the keyword hit, so the timing argument [F3][F4][F5] does not avoid escalation [SAFE-1][SYS-8].

The 'for her own safety' rationale rests only on the driver's own chat statement [F6]; it is a statement, not a system record, and no GPS/timeline fact shows a door open or a moving-vehicle risk, so it cannot be preferred over the record [F6][SYS-3][SAFE-1].
The clean route record is accepted and irrelevant as a defence: it removes a routing/fare issue but says nothing about the disputed words, which independently trigger SAFE-1 [F1][F2][F4][SAFE-1].
Correct that profiles show no pattern, and accepted; but profile facts cannot decide the case either way, so they neither exonerate nor condemn the driver [F7][F8][SYS-9].

Escalation under SAFE-1 does not require proof a lock was engaged; the trigger is threatening language [F4][F5], and the rider's request to exit [F3] is corroborative context, not a precondition [SAFE-1][SYS-8].

Accepted in part as to disposition (escalation, no refund of the $32.86 fixed fare) but rejected as a complete answer: SAFE-1 and SYS-2 forbid a no-inquiry disposition, so the matter must go to human review rather than simply leaving the fare undisturbed [F1][F2][F4][F5][SAFE-1][SYS-2].

Accepted that the message exists and triggers SAFE-1, but rejected as a substantive finding of intent to confine: SYS-8 states keywords only trigger escalation and do not characterise the message, so the outcome is escalation, not a ruling against the driver [F4][F5][SAFE-1][SYS-8].

The temporal sequence is admitted [F3][F4], but chat timing is not a system record of wrongdoing and cannot establish that the rider's exit was obstructed; the question is left to the human reviewer [F3][F4][F6][SYS-3][SAFE-1].

Rejected insofar as it asks the profiles to carry the safety finding: rider and driver histories are both clean and profile facts may not decide the case, so they are corroborative only [F7][F8][SYS-9].

D5 correctly notes there is no alleged overcharge and that the $35.84 RydeX quote is fixed [F1], so no refund is ordered and the amount is null. ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher and flag the driver's "I'm Here" press for abuse review.

The named corridor covers the segment as driven; RD-3(b) is about rider-requested stops and does not deny a driver-proposed, rider-agreed route. rejected_claims.reason: The +5.0 km / +30% aggregate gap [F1] is not itself the unit of review; RD-1 examines each off-route segment, and the only segment [F3] is exempt under RD-5 (F7, F8), so it yields no refundable extra distance [RD-1][RD-2].

Accepted that one off-route segment exists [F3], but existence alone does not decide the case: the segment is exempt under RD-5 because the rider agreed to the named route before the detour [F7][F8][RD-5].

The sequencing argument is met — the agreement at 10:06 [F8] precedes the segment start at 10:09 [F3] — and the consent's scope covers the Ayer Rajah Expressway corridor named in the driver's request [F7]; the 1176 m separation [F3] does not take the drive outside the named corridor. RD-3(b) does not apply to a driver-proposed, rider-agreed route [RD-5][RD-3].

The observation that band 5 [F10] is above the band 1–2 range is true, but it cuts against the rider: with no qualifying incident being credited under RD-4, the segment's disposition turns on RD-5, which the rider fails on [F10][F11][RD-4][RD-5].

The metered-service premise is correct [F6][RD-2], but the per-km rate of $1.41 applies only to non-exempt segments; the sole segment is exempt [F3][F7][F8][RD-5], so no distance units are refundable.
The arithmetic 4.84 km × $1.41 = $6.83 is consistent with [F3][F4], but it presupposes a non-exempt segment; the segment is exempt under RD-5, so the RD-2 amount is $0.00 [RD-2][RD-5].
Correct that no surge [F5] and no waiting charge [F6] exist, but that removes any FARE-1 add-on basis rather than creating a refund; the fare is metered distance and time only [FARE-1][RD-2].
The no-flag conclusion is correct on the profile [F15][RD-6]; the rider's two prior unupheld disputes [F14] cannot independently support any action.

RD-4(a) is not satisfied: the 09:47 breakdown [F12] sits alongside a band 5 (40–49 km/h) record for the same expressway across the segment window [F10], which is not the severe congestion RD-4(b) describes, so the incident does not by itself justify the substitution [RD-4].
Band 5 and band 4 [F10][F11] are not band 1 or 2 and cannot exempt under RD-4(b), which is corroborative only; the driver's reliance on them as exemption grounds fails [RD-4].

The driver's statement [F9] that 'the whole road was slow' is contradicted by the system traffic record for that road (band 5, 40–49 km/h) [F10]; system records override statements, so the statement adds nothing [RD-4].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag on the driver — the wait fell 30 s short of the 3-minute threshold, but the tap was genuine and within the pickup radius.

rejected_claims.reason: The tap itself does not establish the fee: NS-1 requires all three of (i) tap, (ii) GPS presence and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting, and the tap at 14:13:10 was followed by only 1 min 40 s inside the radius before cancellation, so (iii) fails on the system record [F6][F10][NS-1].

The 30-second shortfall is decisive, not a technicality: NS-1(iii) sets a hard threshold of more than 3 minutes, and the system record gives 2 min 30 s within the radius and only 2 min 0 s stationary before the 14:14:50 cancellation, so NS-2 refunds the fee [F2][F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2].
The driver's $4.50 split is irrelevant to the rider's liability; NS-2 makes the full $6.61 refundable once NS-1's conditions are unmet, regardless of how the fee is apportioned [F8][F4][NS-2][NS-7].

Clean profile history does not cure the failed condition: profile facts never decide a case, and NS-1(iii) is measured from the GPS and timeline records, which show a wait below the threshold [F16][F17][F2][NS-1].

The rider's clean profile [F16] is not the basis for the refund; profile facts cannot decide the case, and the outcome follows from the failed wait-duration limb [F16][F2][F3][NS-7].

The no-show finding does not rest on the driver's statement (F12) but on the GPS/timeline record of presence and duration (F1/F2/F3/F5), which the chat merely corroborates; the rider's contrary account has no supporting gps or timeline fact [F2][F3][F12][NS-1].

The driver's profile (F17) cannot decide the case and, per RD-6, additional account action requires the case to be made out against the driver (refund > 0 or an RD-1 breach); here the fee is upheld and the driver was within 200 m when cancelling, so no flag arises [F2][F3][F17][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: NS-0 does route a driver no-show cancellation into NS-1, but all three NS-1 elements pass on the record: tap/arrival at 17:18:50 (F6) with platform arrival logged at 17:17:50 (F5), 38 m from the pickup at the tap with a 34 m closest approach (F6, F1), and 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap before the 17:22:30 cancellation (F6, F4). The framework holds but does not produce the refund the claim seeks [NS-0][NS-1].

F7 (null tap) conflicts with F6 (tap at 17:18:50), and F5 independently records a platform arrival; the more specific arrival record plus the driver's chat (F10) and statement (F12) make NS-1(i) satisfied, so the asserted failure is not established [F7][F6][F5][F10][F12][NS-1][NS-2].

NS-1(ii) is measured against the pickup radius, and the GPS record shows the driver inside 200 m from 17:17:50 for 4 min 40 s with a 34 m closest approach and a 53 m stationary hold (F2, F1, F3). Ryde publishes no arrival radius (gap G2), so 34–53 m satisfies 'at the pick-up location' [F2][F1][F3][NS-1].

NS-2 refunds the $6.61 only if an NS-1 element fails; (i) per F6/F5, (ii) per F1/F2/F3 and (iii) per F6/F4 all pass, so no refund arises and no NS-2 flag attaches (the driver was within range at the tap) [F6][F2][F1][F8][NS-1][NS-2].

The system records favour the driver here rather than the rider: F2 and F5 record arrival within 200 m and F6 records 3 min 40 s of waiting after the tap; the rider's own 'came out a minute after' account has no GPS or timeline fact behind it [F2][F5][F6][F12][NS-1].

The sequence is compliant, not contradictory: 200 m entered at 17:17:50 (F2), stationary hold from 17:18:25 (F3), arrival indication at 17:18:50 (F6), then 3 min 40 s and cancellation at 17:22:30 (F4) — the arrival indication and the wait both precede the cancellation [F2][F3][F6][F4][NS-1].

Traffic is irrelevant to a passenger-no-show cancellation: with no incidents or speed-band records and fair weather (F13, F14, F15), the driver cancelled on the NS-1 gateway, so NS-3 is not engaged and nothing external needs to excuse the fee [F13][F14][F15][NS-3].

Profile facts may only support an additional action and never decide the case; NS-2's flag requires the driver to have tapped 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup range, which F1/F2 refute, and the driver's 90-day record (F17, both no-show matters) does not trigger RD-6 because there is no RD-2 refund and no RD-1 breach here [F16][F17][F1][F2][NS-2][RD-6].

Withdrawn by the rider advocate; to the extent it argues the recorded tap time does not cure NS-1(i), the trace and F6 fix the tap at 17:18:50 with 3 min 40 s of subsequent waiting inside 200 m before the 17:22:30 cancellation, satisfying NS-1(iii) [F6][F7][F4][NS-1].
Accepted only as to the framework and the $6.61 figure; the claim adds nothing to the analysis since payment is governed by NS-1, whose elements are examined via C1–C9 [F4][F8][NS-0][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The fare is metered RydeTAXI, and outside the single unexempted detour segment the trace follows the quoted 15.472 km corridor; only the ~1.72 km off-route mileage plus the metered stop is chargeable above the estimate, so only a partial refund (SGD 2.42) is warranted, not a full fare refund.

rejected_claims.reason: Distance charged (10.761 km) equals the quote (10.761 km) and the GPS trace stays on the quoted polyline; moreover RydeX is a fixed-quote service, so no extra distance could be charged (RD-2 non-metered; FARE-1).

Driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' claim is immaterial: the trace shows the quoted route was followed and the fare is not distance-based; no off-route segment found (RD-1).

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$7.66 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted off-route deviation; no account flag (driver's 90-day route_disputes_upheld = 0, so RD-6 does not apply).

rejected_claims.reason: RydeTAXI is metered; RD-3(c) charges metered waiting units and does not refund them. 1.04 = 4 × 26¢ = 4:00 stationary (14:23:45–14:27:15), matching the rider's own '3-4 minutes' request; NS-6 does not apply to RydeTAXI.
The rider named the place (chat 14:17:00) and the driver agreed before the stop; RD-3(a) treats the passenger-named stop as the destination of that leg, not a deviation.

ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as not upheld; no fare adjustment or refund is due. Optionally send the rider a route/length explanation note.

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $8.20 Ryde voucher (metered-distance overcharge) to the rider; record the driver's violation of the RD-1 shortest-route obligation and remind the driver that route changes require the passenger's agreement BEFORE leaving the optimal route (RD-5).

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.40 Ryde voucher (excess metered distance for the unexempted detour) and record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file; no account flag needed.

Accepted in substance but misdirected: it is true the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and no arrival was recorded [F3][F4], which is exactly why NS-1 earns him nothing; a null timeline cannot be used to keep a fee that NS-4 says is not chargeable [F2].

Absence of chat or misconduct is irrelevant to entitlement: NS-4 makes a cancellation inside 3 minutes non-chargeable without any rider fault [F2][F7], and the driver's statement 'I was on my way' [F8] is a statement that yields to the timeline records [F2][F3][F4].

Conceded and neutral: normal traffic, no incidents and fair weather [F9][F10][F11] mean the driver was simply driving [F1], which rebuts any fabricated-arrival allegation but supplies no NS-1 or NS-3 basis for charging the rider.

The amount is arithmetically $6.61 with no surge [F5][F6], but arithmetic correctness is not entitlement; NS-4 charges nothing inside the 3-minute window [F2], and NS-7 supplies the voucher/30-day route, not a basis to keep the fee.

Accepted as to profile: F13 cannot decide the case and no flag applies since there was no 'I'm Here' tap and no trip completed without a rider [F4]; this disposes of the rider's C6 add-on, not of the refund itself [F2][F5].

The profile facts (3 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show) [F13] cannot ground an account action here: NS-2's flag limb requires an 'I'm Here' tap while off-location and there was no tap at all [F4], and RD-6 does not apply because this is not a route-deviation case with an RD-2 refund.

The driver's statement [F14] and clean record [F19] cannot establish that NS-1 is satisfied; profile facts never decide a case, and the NS-1(i) conflict [F6][F7] is untouched by either [NS-1].

Dispute histories [F18][F19] cannot decide or weight the fee; profile facts are context only, and the driver side itself withdrew this line [NS-1].

The driver's position that SAFE-1 escalation leaves the fee finding intact [F12][F13][F1][F2][F3][F6] fails because escalation means no merits finding is made at this stage, and the NS-1(i) limb is unresolved [F6][F7][NS-1][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider treats 181 m as proof the driver was 'not at the pick-up location', but no clause publishes a pin-exact or metre test for NS-1(ii) [RD-NS-1]; the 200 m radius is a data-layer parameter (gap G2), and the system record shows the driver inside that recorded range at the tap and throughout [F2][F6], so the position limb passes.

The retreat to 181 m and stationary hold [F3] is a position-and-duration fact that satisfies NS-1(iii) rather than defeating it: the driver remained inside the recorded pick-up range for 3 min 40 s after the tap [F6][F2], more than the 3:01 required by NS-1 [RD-NS-1].

NS-2 only bites where an NS-1 limb fails [RD-NS-2]; all three limbs are met on the system record — tap at 14:07:40 [F6], inside range at that moment [F1][F6], and over 3 minutes of waiting after it [F6][F2] — so no full refund of $6.61 arises.

The rider being reachable at the entrance [F11] does not displace NS-1: the driver gave his waiting position at 14:07 [F10] and cancelled only after the wait threshold had elapsed [F12][F4], which is the NS-1 scenario, not NS-2 [RD-NS-1][RD-NS-2].

Correct as stated but immaterial: profile facts never decide the case, and the driver's clean history [F18] neither establishes nor defeats the fee, which turns on the NS-1 records, not on RD-6 [RD-RD-6].

RD-4 governs justification for a reroute and is not a condition of NS-1 [RD-RD-4]; the absence of incidents, speed bands and rain [F14][F15][F16] simply means no exemption or excuse is in issue, leaving the NS-1 analysis undisturbed.

The driver's point that $6.61 with no surge [F8][F9] is the published amount is factually true but not decisive by itself; the fee stands because NS-1 is satisfied [RD-NS-1], not because the figure matches the tariff.

The rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days [F17] cannot be used to establish this breach; profile facts are relevant only to an ancillary account action and never decide the main finding [RD-RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human review as a SAFE-1 safety/threat incident: provide the reviewer the verbatim chat log (F3–F5), the driver's statement (F6), the route/duration records (F1, F2) and both profiles (F7, F8); take no fare or account action automatically. Reviewer to determine (a) whether the 17:20 message was a genuine threat to confine the rider, and (b) any account consequence. Note the rider's recourse if medical assistance or a police report is needed (995 / RydeHELP) [SAFE-2 context].
ruling.escalation_reason: Threat-tagged driver chat message in a rider-filed safety dispute: chat #2 17:20 "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], keyword-tagged as a threat [F5], sent one minute after the rider's 17:19 request to stop and get out [F3]; driver's account is that it was a safety instruction during a moving-vehicle door incident [F6]. No gps/timeline fact records locked doors or a stationary vehicle; route and duration records are normal (−0.1 km vs optimal [F1], +1.4 min [F2]). Reviewer to check: (1) whether the 17:20 message is a genuine threat to confine the rider; (2) any corroborating records (door/vehicle sensors, timeline events) for the driver's account in F6; (3) account consequences for either party given both profiles are clean [F7][F8]; no fare adjustment arises ($32.86 fixed RydeX fare, no deviation).

rejected_claims.reason: Rejected as a basis for adjudication: the driver's safety motive [F6] is a statement and under the system-records-prevail rule cannot override the verbatim chat message [F4] and its threat tag [F5]; in any event SAFE-1 escalates on the presence of a threat message in the record without weighing the stated motive.

Rejected as irrelevant to the safety claim: a non-aberrant route and normal duration [F1][F2] do not neutralize a threat-tagged chat message [F4][F5], and SAFE-1 attaches to the chat record, not to gps route metrics.

Rejected as irrelevant: no fare or route complaint arises here — the trip ran to the booked destination with actual 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal [F1][F2] and the RydeX fare is fixed so no RD-2 refund exists; the escalatable conduct is the 17:20 threat message [F4][F5], which RD-3/FARE-1 do not address.

Rejected only as to the requested outcome: the driver's clean 90-day record with 0 upheld disputes [F8] does not bar escalation, because RD-6's prior-upheld precondition is about repeated-violation flags, and SAFE-1 requires escalation on a single threat-tagged message [F4][F5]; no flag_account is imposed in any case.
Rejected only as to the requested outcome: the rider's clean profile [F7] removes any vexatious-claim suggestion but does not counteract the SAFE-1 escalation trigger in the chat record [F4][F5].

Not adopted as a finding: the 'confinement as leverage' reading is an inference beyond the record — the only record is the message itself [F4] with its tag [F5], and no gps/timeline fact shows locked doors or a held vehicle [F1][F2]; the weight of that inference is for the human reviewer under SAFE-1, not for this escalation summary.

Adopted as to the procedural outcome (escalate under SAFE-1 on threat message [F4][F5]) but its further assertion that a fare adjustment question exists is rejected: route is optimal at 15.4 km vs 15.5 km [F1] and the RydeX fare is fixed, so RD-2 yields no refundable amount.

Adopted as to scope: the driver has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F8], so the RD-6 repeated-breach precondition is not met and no flag_account is issued; any account review rests on this single escalated safety incident under SAFE-1.

But her message asked only for a 3–4 minute parcel stop, and her own words do not agree to any unnamed 3.80 km / 9-minute excursion; the stationary time at the stop is only 4 min 0 s, which accounts for the end of the segment, not the whole of it [F9][F2]. rejected_claims.reason: The rider's premise that the whole detour segment falls outside her consent is only partly right: she named the place Clementi Mall in her own pre-segment message, and the car stopped there, so under RD-3(a) the way to the named stop (including the on-route approach to it) is exempt rather than counted — the 1.70 km cannot simply be treated as an unconsented route change in full [F9][F10][F2][F4][RD-3].

The driver's RD-3(a)/RD-5 defence fails in scope. The rider's 14:17 message names a place and a 3–4 minute errand, not the 3.80 km / 9-minute excursion the GPS records [F9][F4], so the exemption covers reaching the named stop but not the driver's choice of a longer, unnamed route; a driver's post-trip statement cannot supply the missing consent (G11) [F12][F9][F4][RD-3][RD-5].

The absence of a recorded incident [F15] does not exonerate the driver: it merely removes the RD-4 reasonable-cause defence, leaving the segments to be judged under RD-3/RD-5, where only the named-stop portion is exempt [F15][F9][F4][RD-4][RD-3][RD-5].

Accepted that the refund must be computed from the segment figures (1.70 km) and not the whole $25.52 total [F4][F8][RD-2]; applied accordingly — the refund is $2.40, and the $0.25 mapping residual is not refundable [F5][F1][RD-2].

RD-3(a) also fails: 'a 7-Eleven' is a brand, not a specific place named by the rider, and the store used lay off the optimal route; RD-3(b) therefore applies and the segment's extra 3.17 km is not exempted by the stop request. The 4 min 10 s stationary period is the rider-requested stop itself — the rider asked for a 7-Eleven stop of about 2 minutes [F9] and the driver accepted [F10]. Accepted on the facts but it defeats the driver's own position: the driver confirms the chosen store was off the optimal route and was never identified in the chat [F4][F9][F12], which is exactly the RD-3(b) finding that the stop request does not exempt the route change.

Route and fare are undisputed: 8.8 km vs 8.9 km optimal and 13.3 min vs 16 min estimated [F1][F2], metered fare $21.26 untouched; no RD-2 refund and no RD-1 breach, so RD-6's flag_account gateway is not met [F7][F8]. Reviewer should assess the rider's message under the Code of Conduct and decide any account action.

rejected_claims.reason: Correctly states there was no unexplained extra distance or time [F1][F2], and I adopt that; but C4's framing of the case as a fare question is rejected in its only operative part — a safety threat in the chat [F4][F5] is not disposed of by the absence of a deviation, and it triggers escalation under SAFE-1 rather than any refund or fee adjustment under RD-1/RD-2.

Accepted: no repeated-violation pattern exists on either profile, so RD-6's flag_account gateway is not open [F7][F8][RD-6]. The claim is retained only in this negative sense; it cannot be used to suggest the safety report lacks merit, since F7/F8 are profile facts and profile facts never decide a case [RD-6].

Accepted as to the chat record being complete and timestamped [F5][F3][F4][F6], and as to the SAFE-1 consequence; but D2's citation of RD-5 is rejected — RD-5 governs a rider's pre-departure consent to a driver-proposed route change, and there is no route deviation and no consent question on this trip [F1][F2][RD-1].

Accepted as to the driver's clean history [F8] and as to profile facts being incapable of deciding the case; but the implied request that the rider's account be reviewed as a penalty is rejected — RD-6 requires an upheld case against the driver plus a repeated-breach profile, neither of which exists [F1][F2][F7][F8][RD-6], and D5 itself concedes no flag_account is sought.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; close the rider's waiver request and inform the rider that the fee stands (NS-7 voucher route not applicable). No account action.

rejected_claims.reason: F7 (driver_pressed_here_at null) cannot establish that NS-1(i) failed. NS-1(i) is satisfied by the platform-confirmed arrival/press at 14:07:40 [F6], which the operational records corroborate [F2][F5], and F7's flat 'never tapped' is contradicted by those records and by the driver's timestamped on-scene message [F10]. An internally impossible record cannot defeat a fee the system records otherwise support; NS-1(i) stands, so NS-2 is not triggered.

The arithmetic fails. Even on the rider's own preferred tap time of 14:07:40, the driver stayed continuously inside the 200 m radius for 3 min 40 s (220 s) until the 14:11:20 cancellation [F6][F3][F4], which exceeds the 180 s required by NS-1(iii); on the platform arrival record the wait was 4 min 40 s (280 s) [F2][F5]. The driver's summary phrase 'waited more than 3 min' [F12] describes his own count, not a shorter wait.

The rider's message at 14:09 [F11] shows she was present and looking, but presence of the rider does not defeat NS-1: the fee turns on the driver's press, GPS location and waiting time, all satisfied here [F6][F1][F2][F5]. She was told the car's exact position and model at 14:07 [F10] and the driver remained stationary at that announced spot until cancelling [F3][F12].

Correct that the post-trip statement [F14] is a mere claim, but it is not the basis of my finding. The fee is sustained by the system records F6/F2/F5 and the timestamped chat F10, not by F14; the alleged contradiction with F3 is answered because F3 records the stand at the driver's announced side-road position 181 m from the pin, still inside the NS-1(ii) radius [F1][F6].

NS-1(ii) requires GPS to show the driver at the pick-up location, and the operative parameter is proximity to the pick-up point (200 m), not parking at the pin: 181 m at the tap and 60 m closest approach satisfy it [F1][F3][F6]. The rider was given the exact position and car [F10] and never asked the driver to move [F11][F13], so the alleged relocation of the pick-up point did not deprive the fee of its NS-1 basis. NS-3 is not engaged because the driver does allege and does satisfy rider no-show under NS-1.

Conceded and irrelevant. Traffic and weather records [F15][F16][F17] bear on RD-4 excuses for route deviation, not on NS-1, which turns only on the here-press, GPS location and waiting time [F6][F2][F5].

NS-2's full refund arises only if a limb of NS-1 fails; none does [F6][F1][F2][F5], so the $6.61 on the fare record stands [F8][F4]. The rider's clean 90-day history [F18] is a profile fact and, under the profile rule, cannot alone decide a case either way.

No flag. NS-2's flag attaches where the driver presses 'I'm Here' while GPS shows he is not at the pick-up; here GPS places him inside the radius from 14:06:40 to cancellation [F2][F5]. RD-6 is inapplicable to a no-show fee dispute and requires an upheld RD-2 refund or a recorded RD-1 breach, neither of which exists; the driver's two prior upheld no-show disputes [F19] are profile facts and cannot alone support an account action.
Accepted only insofar as the safety screen is none [F10][F11][F12][F14]; this is a factual concession, not a clause bearing on the outcome under NS-1.

ruling.escalation_reason: Rider reports dangerous driving (speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder) and states she felt scared and unsafe; the driver denies it in a post-trip written statement. The chat gives no contemporaneous safety message and the GPS record contains only distance and duration, no speed, acceleration or lane-position data, so the conflict cannot be resolved on this record and SAFE-2 routes it to a human reviewer.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the 0.1 km shorter distance establishes there was 'no violation to record' misuses RD-1: RD-1 governs route deviation, and the ride had no off-route segment [F1]; it says nothing about the speed and lane-position allegations, which are decided under SAFE-2, not RD-1 [F1][F2][RD-1][SAFE-2].

The assertion that 12.8 min against a 14 min estimate 'contradicts' the erratic-driving account reads a duration fact for more than it says; the record contains no speed or braking data, so the figure neither corroborates nor contradicts the allegation [F2][SAFE-2].

The absence of a chat complaint does not disprove a safety allegation: the chat is complete and shows only pickup logistics [F3][F4][F5], and no policy clause makes an in-app message a precondition for a valid dangerous-driving report, which SAFE-2 sends to a human regardless [F5][SAFE-2].

The driver's clean profile [F8] cannot weigh against the conduct alleged on this ride, and RD-6 concerns route-deviation sanctions and account flags, not dangerous-driving referrals; profile facts never decide a case and no flag is supported here [F7][F8][RD-6].

The conclusion (escalate) is correct but the supporting facts do not bear it: F3–F5 are pickup-logistics messages containing no safety content, so SAFE-2 attaches on the complaint's dangerous-driving allegation, not on those chat facts [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-2].

The claim that the 12.8 min / 8.5 km figures are 'exactly the profile of a fast run' over-reads the record; the GPS facts record distance and duration only, and neither corroborates nor refutes the alleged speeding and hard braking [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

The submission that the driver's statement 'cannot outweigh' the rider's safety report asks the adjudicator to resolve a credibility conflict on the papers; there is no contemporaneous rider safety report either, and the untimestamped denial is one side of an unresolved conflict that SAFE-2 sends to a human [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-2].

Correct on the fare — the fixed $21.04 quote stands with no excess distance billed [F1][FARE-1][RD-2] — but RD-2 is a refund formula and no refund is sought or computed, so it adds nothing to the safety referral.

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer with the fact summary; read the rider's full complaint text and interview both parties before any finding — no refund is computed on this record
ruling.escalation_reason: Rider alleges harassment / unwanted personal advances (comments about her body, request for her number) during the ride [F3][F4]. SAFE-1 makes such an allegation a screening matter for a human, not an automatic ruling. The conduct is spoken, so no chat, gps or fare record captures it: the chat record is empty [F3], the driver's denial is a statement made after the trip [F4], and the trip data are unremarkable [F1][F2]. The record cannot settle the question; a person must read the complaint and interview both parties.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that nothing in the record rises to a harassment-type allegation requiring escalation fails: SAFE-1 is triggered by the allegation as stated, which the driver's own advocate concedes must be screened, and the rider's complaint describes repeated comments about her body and a request for her number, an unwanted-advances allegation on its face [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. Escalation does not require the conduct to be pre-recorded in the chat [F3] or conceded in the driver's statement [F4].

The claim that the normal gps trace (17.2 km vs 17.3 km optimal [F1]; 25.9 min vs 24 min estimate [F2]) shows no misconduct cannot defeat the allegation: route and duration data say nothing about what was said inside the cabin, and the driver's statement that 'nothing inappropriate happened' [F4] is a statement, not a system record, so it does not displace the rider's account [SAFE-1].

The claim that the driver's clean profile (4.5 y, rating 4.86, 659 trips, 0 disputes in 90 d [F6]) resolves the case fails: profile facts cannot decide a safety allegation alone, and a first-time allegation against a long-standing account is exactly what SAFE-1 sends to a human [F6][SAFE-1].

The point that both parties' clean profiles (rider 3.8 y, rating 4.8, 0 disputes in 90 d [F5]; driver [F6]) show no history of baseless complaints is accepted only as non-decisive context; profile facts cannot by themselves establish or negate the harassment allegation, so they yield no ruling either way [F5][F6][SAFE-1].

The framing of the empty chat record as itself weighted evidence ('the harassment was not denied in writing during the trip') is not sustainable: an empty chat log [F3] is an absence of data, and under the record-reading rules an absence cannot be counted for either side; the safety question must be read from the complaint text by a person [F3][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a RydeHELP human reviewer as a dangerous-driving (SAFE-2) case: attach the rider's complaint, the complete chat [F3][F4][F5], and the driver's post-trip statement [F6]; advise the rider of the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting path [SAFE-2]; do not adjust the $24.76 fixed RydeX fare in the automated layer.
ruling.escalation_reason: Dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) made by the rider; the file contains only distance/duration records with no speed, acceleration or lane-position data, and a complete, timestamped chat with no mid-trip message. Under SAFE-2 the case must go to a human with this summary; the driver's insulting post-trip note [F6] is a credibility matter, not an independent threat under SAFE-1.

rejected_claims.reason: F1/F2 show only total distance (10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal) and total duration (16.1 min vs 16 min) and contain no speed, acceleration or lane-position data, so they cannot affirmatively disprove the alleged speeding and hard braking; the record merely fails to corroborate it, which is why the case escalates rather than closes [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

Correct that the rider's account is uncorroborated by any system fact [F3][F4][F5], but lack of corroboration is not a reason to rule against the rider on a dangerous-driving allegation: SAFE-2 requires the case be sent to a person, and F6 is itself an entry in the record [F6][SAFE-2].

The absence of a mid-trip message in a complete, timestamped chat [F3][F4][F5] is equally consistent with a frightened rider not typing during the ride; it is not evidence that nothing happened and carries no exonerating weight [F5][SAFE-2].

Profile facts (820 d, 4.72 rating, 455 trips, 0 disputes) [F8] never decide a case alone and say nothing about the driving conduct on this trip; they neither rebut nor support the rider's account [F8][SAFE-1].

The driver's request for escalate is granted, and indeed is the only permitted disposition, but his framing that the file shows 'no evidence of the driving pattern alleged' [F1][F2] misreads the records: they are silent on speed, braking and shoulder use rather than exculpatory [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

The rider and driver both ask for escalation under SAFE-2 and I so rule; but this is a screening outcome, not a finding that the driving complaint is substantiated, which the file cannot establish [F1][F2][F5][SAFE-2].

The driver's post-trip remark calling the rider 'stupid' [F6] is insulting and weighs on his credibility before the human reviewer, but on reading the words in context it is not a threat, intimidation, harassment or sexual remark, so it is not itself a SAFE-1 safety event [F6][SAFE-1].

The rider's own arithmetic (about 39 km/h average) built on F1/F2 does not rehabilitate the allegation: an average speed cannot establish speed spikes, harsh braking or shoulder overtaking, none of which any record captures [F1][F2][RD-1].

The rider's clean 90-day history (661 d account, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) [F7] and the driver's history [F8] are profile facts that cannot decide the case, and the complete chat [F3][F4][F5] being silent on the driving is neutral, not corroborative of either account [F5][F7][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $1.09 Ryde voucher refund for the unexempted 0.77 km of metered distance on the 09:49–09:52 off-route segment; record the RD-1 shortest-direct-route breach on the driver's file; no account flag.

segment_findings.reason: The 09:49–09:52 off-route segment added 0.77 km and strayed up to 1019 m from the optimal route [F3]. No rider message before 09:49 agrees to any route the driver named: the only rider message is the 09:35 lobby/red-jacket pickup note [F7][F8], and the driver's post-trip statement of GPS rerouting is a claim, not consent [F9], so RD-5 gives no exemption [F7][F9][RD-5]. Nor is there any rider-named stop in this segment, so RD-3(a) does not apply [F7][F3][RD-3]. RD-4 offers no excuse: no incident was recorded [F12] and the only traffic readings are band 4, which neither meets RD-4(b) nor exempts a segment alone [F10][F11][RD-4]. The segment's 0.77 km is therefore refundable under RD-2 [F3][F6][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted in substance, but its RD-1 breach framing is only the premise: the refund is capped by RD-2 at the unexempted segment's extra_km, which is 0.77 km, not the full deviation [F3][RD-1][RD-2].
The +1.6 km / +15% whole-trip figure [F1] cannot enlarge the refund: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km of 0.77 km [F3][F1][RD-2].
Accepted; the segment is refundable at 0.77 km × $1.41/km [F3][F6][RD-2], which is the amount awarded.
Accepted; the absence of any incident [F12] is why RD-4(a) does not exempt the segment [F12][RD-4].
Accepted; band 4 is not a band 1/2 reading and a band record alone does not exempt, so RD-4(b) does not excuse the segment [F10][F11][RD-4].
Accepted; fair weather [F13] removes any weather-related reasonable cause under RD-4 [F13][RD-4].
Accepted; the complete timestamped chat [F8] shows no pre-09:49 rider consent [F7], so RD-5 does not exempt the segment [F7][RD-5].
Accepted; the driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not consent or traffic evidence, and RD-4 requires incident evidence that is absent [F9][F12][RD-5][RD-4].
Accepted; route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15], so RD-6's precondition for a flag is not met and no account action attaches [F15][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only message before the segment asks to 'stop at a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming any store or location [F9], and the driver simply said 'Ok' [F10]; the driver's own after-the-trip statement, 'I went to the one I know' [F12], shows the store was his choice, so there is no rider message naming a place (RD-3(a) not met, RD-3(b) applies) and no rider message naming a road or area agreed before 17:37 (RD-5 not met). rejected_claims.reason: The rider's 17:33 message [F9] asks for a stop only and names no place; RD-3(a) exempts a stop only where the rider named the place or the chosen place lay on the optimal route, and here the chosen store produced the off-route segment in [F4], so the request as worded does not exempt the route taken.

RD-3(b) expressly provides that an unnamed-place stop whose chosen location creates an off-route segment is not exempt, and RD-5 requires a rider message naming the road or area before the segment started; the only basis for the store's location is the driver's post-trip statement [F12], which is a claim, not consent.

FARE-1 addresses unpublished add-on items, and the fare breakdown [F8] contains none; it does not displace RD-2, whose RydeTAXI branch exists precisely because a metered fare rises with distance, so the 3.17 km non-exempt segment [F4] is still payable back to the rider.

RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days to make this a repeated breach, and the driver's record shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F18]; the account-flag limb is not satisfied, and the rider advocate withdrew it.

The record holds no chat [F7]; the complaint (driver "was nowhere near") and the driver's statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F8] are fare/no-show dispute language, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. rejected_claims.reason: The refund half of C5 is granted, but the requested account flag is rejected: NS-2's flag requires that the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him away from the pickup, and the timeline shows he never pressed it, so the abuse-of-button trigger does not exist [F4][F1][NS-2]. The driver's profile (1 upheld dispute in 90 days, 1,160 trips) cannot support flagging on its own [F13][NS-2].

D3's outcome (full refund under NS-2) is superseded: NS-2 applies only to driver-cancellation no-show claims, whereas the rider cancelled here, so the fee falls under NS-4's 3-minute rule [F2][F5][NS-0][NS-4]. Its rejection of any flag is accepted [F4][NS-2].

Only the assertion that the driver's statement is "independently disproved as to his intention" is rejected; the operative point stands — the statement asserts no rider no-show and is overridden by the GPS and timeline records [F8][F1][F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer with the factual summary; do not auto-adjudicate or levy any fee/refund; reviewer to read the 17:19–17:20 exchange and the driver's post-trip statement, and to decide whether the conduct warrants a Code of Conduct review. Safety reporting path (RydeHELP) to be relayed to the rider.
ruling.escalation_reason: Rider complaint of feeling unsafe and of being threatened with being locked in, supported by the driver's contemporaneous message "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4] sent at 17:20 in reply to the rider's 17:19 request to stop and get out [F3], during a ride in progress [F2]. The driver's explanation that this was a safety instruction because the rider tried to open the door while moving appears only in his post-trip statement [F6] and is not corroborated by any gps or timeline fact [F1][F2]. Chat record is complete and timestamped [F5]. No routing, duration or fare anomaly is in dispute (15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal, 23.2 min vs 22 min estimated) [F1][F2]. Human reviewer should read F3/F4 verbatim and obtain the driver's account of the door episode and whether the vehicle was moving at the time; consider whether continuing the trip for roughly 11 minutes after the rider's exit request was itself unsafe. Profiles (rider 709 d / 4.8 rating / 0 disputes; driver 510 d / 4.66 rating / 786 trips / 0 disputes) do not decide this and are neutral on the threat question [F7][F8].

rejected_claims.reason: The words and their timing are undisputed (17:19 rider request [F3], 17:20 driver reply [F4], trip in progress [F2]), but the characterisation of F4 as a threat is precisely the reading SAFE-1 reserves for a human; the automated ruling cannot adopt it.
Rider profile facts (709 d, 4.8, 0 disputes) [F7] cannot decide the case and are neutral on whether F4 was a threat; the driver's statement [F6] is an explanation, not an admission of a threat.

The timing/status of F6 as a post-trip statement is noted, but it is not contradicted by any system record [F1][F2], so it cannot be dismissed as false on this record; the question it bears on goes to the human reviewer.
The absence of a routing or fare anomaly [F1][F2] does not bear on the conduct allegation; the referral under SAFE-1 rests on the chat words [F3][F4], not on trip uneventfulness.

Describing F4 as a mere instruction to remain seated is one reading of the words; read with the message that prompted it [F3], a conditional consequence attached to a request to exit is capable of being coercive, so this reading cannot be adopted as the automated finding either way.
The completeness and timestamping of the chat [F5] does not establish that no threat occurred; the record contains the driver's conditional words [F4], which is what SAFE-1 sends to a human.

rejected_claims.reason: NS-2's abuse-of-the-button flag requires GPS to show the driver outside the pickup area when he tapped; F6 (181 m) and F2 (inside the radius from 14:06:40) show the opposite, so the tap was within range, not abusive [F6][F2][NS-2][NS-1].
Conceded geography does not decide the case: F3/F1 show a stand-off from the pin, but NS-1 turns on the arrival radius and the wait duration, both satisfied by F6 and F2 [F3][F1][F6][F2][NS-1].
Condition (ii) of NS-1 is met on the measured record — 181 m at the tap, inside the 200 m range, per F6 and F2 — so the fee is valid and NS-2's refund trigger is not reached [F6][F2][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

F10 shows the rider was near the pin looking for the car, but presence at the pin is not boarding; NS-1 requires the driver to have waited over 3 minutes at the pickup, which F3/F6/F5 establish, so the fee stands [F10][F3][F6][F5][NS-1].

The driver's statement F13 is not needed: F6, F3 and F5 independently record the tap, the stationary wait and the cancellation timing, so striking the statement leaves the NS-1 findings intact [F13][F6][F3][F5][NS-1].

An NS-2 account flag requires GPS placing the driver outside the pickup area at the tap; F6/F2 place him inside, and F18 is a profile fact that under NS-2/RD-6 can only support an additional action, never create the finding [F6][F2][F18][NS-2][RD-6].

The $6.61 is validly charged under NS-1 because (i), (ii) and (iii) are all met on the system record (F6, F2, F3, F4), so there is no refundable sum under NS-2 and NS-7 [F7][F6][F2][F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2][NS-7].
Accepted in outcome but not on the driver's reasoning: the fee stands on the NS-1 elements, not on his statement F13, which the GPS distance facts partially contradict [F13][F1][F3][NS-1][NS-2].

ruling.escalation_reason: Rider alleges sexual harassment by the driver during the trip (comments about her body, request for her number, feeling unsafe) — a SAFE-1 Code of Conduct matter that must not be auto-adjudicated. The chat record is empty (F3) and the driver's only response is his own untimed post-trip denial (F4), so both accounts rest on assertion. GPS shows no deviation and no dangerous driving (F1, F2). Human reviewer should read the rider's complaint, put the account to the driver, and seek any evidence outside this file (device telemetry, prior complaints, other riders) before any finding.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's inference that the empty chat log leaves the harassment account unrebutted proves nothing on its own: the absence of in-app messages is neutral, not corroborative, and cannot substitute for the missing evidence of the cabin conversation [F3][SAFE-1].

The rider's reading that the normal GPS track leaves driver conduct as 'the only disputed issue' is accepted only in part — F1 and F2 show no deviation and no dangerous driving, so no monetary or route finding follows from them [F1][F2][SAFE-2].
The clean profiles (F5, F6) cannot support any finding for the rider: profile facts never decide a case and here they establish no pattern on either side [F5][F6][SAFE-1][RD-6].

The driver's inference that the empty chat log means no remarks were made is rejected: an empty record is not exculpatory, and the driver's own statement confirms a conversation took place [F3][F4][SAFE-1].
The driver's denial (F4) is his own untimed post-trip statement, an assertion rather than a system record, and cannot outweigh the rider's account or decide the central disputed fact [F4][SAFE-1].
The driver's reliance on his clean history to close the matter is rejected: F6 supports no account-level sanction and cannot be used to resolve the harassment allegation itself [F6][SAFE-1][RD-6].

The driver's point that there is no contested charge is correct as far as the fixed fare goes (F1, FARE-1), but it does not dispose of the safety allegation, which is remitted to human review [F1][FARE-1][SAFE-1].

ruling.escalation_reason: Rider reports dangerous driving (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking, feeling unsafe), which SAFE-2 routes to a human; no system record in the file (GPS distance 8.5 km vs 8.6 km optimal [F1]; 12.8 min vs 14 min estimate [F2]) records or excludes instantaneous driving conduct, and the complete timestamped chat [F3][F4][F5] contains no in-trip complaint, so the allegation cannot be settled from the record.

rejected_claims.reason: The inference that F1/F2 disprove sustained speeding/hard driving is rejected: GPS records total distance 8.5 km vs 8.6 km optimal [F1] and total duration 12.8 min vs 14 min estimate [F2], which measure distance and time only and say nothing about instantaneous speed, acceleration or braking; a dangerous-driving allegation under SAFE-2 is escalated, not dismissed on such records (SAFE-2).

The absence of any GPS/timeline/fare/traffic fact recording a shoulder manoeuvre, harsh braking or an unsafe event is an evidentiary gap, not proof the allegation is false; missing evidence is not read in either party's favour, and the trace directs escalation where the record cannot settle the issue (SAFE-2, SAFE-1).

The complete timestamped chat holding only the rider's pickup message [F3] and the driver's arrival message [F4] shows only that no safety message was exchanged [F5]; neither SAFE-1 nor SAFE-2 makes an in-app in-trip complaint a precondition for a safety report (SAFE-1, SAFE-2).

The driver's post-trip statement 'I drove normally' [F6] is a claim, not a system record and not part of the chat, so it cannot resolve a contested driving-conduct allegation in the driver's favour; statement-versus-complaint cannot be settled on this record (SAFE-1).

The driver's profile (1263 d, 4.82 rating, 345 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d) [F8] is background only and cannot decide the case; in any event no account flag is available here because there is no upheld finding and thus no RD-6 predicate (RD-6).

The rider's profile (1308 d, 4.5, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d) [F7] is likewise background only and cannot decide the merits; the outcome follows from the safety-screen routing of the dangerous-driving allegation, not from either party's history (SAFE-1, SAFE-2).

Conceded and accepted: with 8.5 km actual against 8.6 km optimal [F1], there is no off-route segment and no excess distance, so no RD-2 refund and no amount arise, and RD-1's shortest-route duty is not breached on these records (RD-1, RD-2).

The 3 min 30 s stationary period [F2] satisfies NS-1(iii) only in duration, not in place: the entire wait was 600 m from the pickup point and the driver spent 0 s inside the radius after the tap [F5], so the wait was not 'at the pick-up point' as NS-1(iii) requires.

The 12:06 message 'I'm here already' [F8] is disproved by the GPS record [F1][F2][F5], so the mismatch was caused by the driver's position, not by any rider no-show; the rider's reply [F9] matches the system record and NS-1 requires a location the driver never reached.

Not contested and irrelevant to liability: charging exactly the published $6.61 with 1.0× surge [F6][F7] does not cure the failure of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii), which under NS-2 requires the full fee to be refunded.

Withdrawn in rebuttal and in any case ineffective: the driver's clean profile (873 d, 4.84, 502 trips, 0 upheld) [F17] cannot excuse the off-location arrival tap shown by the system record [F5][F1][F4], which NS-2 makes the basis for flag_account; profile facts never decide a case alone.
