segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment(s) between pickup (09:03) and dropoff: the trace sits well south of the quoted CTE corridor (loop to Marina/Shenton Way) and the thinned GPS (30 s grid, holes up to 8 min, trace not covering the trip start) does not allow segment boundaries or extra_km to be established; no RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 exemption applies (empty chat, no incident, band-only traffic that does not cover the segment). Undetermined per G12/G13; because it changes the RD-2 amount, escalate.

rejected_claims.reason: Claims AYE was crawling/flooding; the only traffic record (speed band 2 on AYE, window 08:49:50–09:12:10) does not cover the driven segment and RD-4(b) bands cannot exempt on their own; no traffic-incident fact exists (incidents = []). Driver's assertion alone cannot establish 'reasonable cause' under RD-4(c).
Any implication that the rider accepted the detour is a claim in the driver's statement only; chat is empty, so there is no rider-consent message before the deviation (RD-5; G11).

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $2.06 to the rider for the metered distance overcharge caused by the unexplained off-route stretch on the PIE (RD-2); note on the driver's file that the extra distance was not justified by the rider's named stop at Paya Lebar Square, and re-confirm the route before any mid-trip stop so the detour is charged to the rider only if agreed.

segment_findings.reason: ~1.5 km off-route loop on the PIE between 12:19:20 and 12:20:20 (the plotted fastest route has no such loop) occurring BEFORE the Paya Lebar Square stop and not leading toward it; the named-stop exemption (RD-3(a)) does not cover it, it was not announced/agreed before the deviation (RD-5), and there is no traffic incident or band 1/2 corroboration (RD-4) → unexempted under RD-1, refunded per RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's 'detour' claim cannot be read as covering the whole trip. The main deviation — the ~7 km run to Paya Lebar Square and back — was the rider's own named request (chat 12:20:55, accepted by the driver), exempt under RD-3(a); only 1.5 km of the detour is refundable, not the full fare difference.

The driver's account of the stop at Paya Lebar Square is consistent with the GPS (stationary 12:28:50–12:31:50) and is accepted, but it is irrelevant to the pre-stop PIE loop, which no party's message covers.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$3.32 (metered-distance overcharge for the unexempted off-route segment) to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7/RD-2; remind the driver that a mid-trip stop must be at a location on or near the shortest route or the rider must be told the specific stop in advance (RD-3(b), RD-5). No account flag (no prior upheld route dispute, RD-6 not met).

segment_findings.reason: GPS trace leaves the quoted route at 1.3162,103.8887 (~17:40:40) and rejoins at 1.3245,103.8907 (~17:48:10), running ~2.3 km off the quote (via 1.3135,103.8884 where the car stood for 2-3 min for the 7-Eleven stop). No traffic incident (RD-4(a) fails) and the route's speed bands are band 4 (RD-4(b) cannot exempt). Under RD-3(b) the rider asked only for 'a 7-Eleven on the way', named no location, and the driver never told the rider which store, so the extra distance is not covered by the stop request; RD-5 consent (general route licence does not cover a driver's own errand/stop) does not extend to it. Off-route, unexempted → counts under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: RydeTAXI is metered (A18); the metre fare (S$41.17) legitimately exceeds the fixed-quote estimate (S$32.09) because distance/time are billed by the metre, not the quote. Only the unexempted detour distance is refundable (RD-2), which is S$3.32.

rejected_claims.id: driver: rider agreed to the store
rejected_claims.reason: No rider message names or approves the specific store; the chat only shows 'a 7-Eleven on the way'. The driver's statement that he went 'to the one I know' is not consent (G11); the detour distance is therefore not exempt under RD-3/RD-5.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.61 (voucher per NS-7) for the off-route metered distance and send the driver's record to Ryde account review (repeated upheld route-deviation case) + flag_account

segment_findings.reason: Off-route running 14:27:45-14:37:15: north of the AYE via Bukit Timah/Kent Ridge up to ~1.3057/103.7688, then the AYE eastward past the NUS-nearest point and the doubling-back leg to NUS. The rider's message designates only the Clementi Mall stop (RD-3(a)); the record does not tie the post-stop re-route to it, but the 6th-sample 30 s trace over-reports distance at 40+ km/h samples so the split of the 1.98 km meter excess between the exempt named-stop approach and this counted leg cannot be fixed. Affects the amount (S$2.4-2.9 band) but not the ruling or the flag.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's account stops at 'drove there and waited'; it does not explain the post-stop northing and the AYE run past the NUS-nearest point, and a driver's assertion of consent or purpose is not consent (G11). System GPS overrides it.

Only partly right: the named Clementi Mall stop itself is exempt under RD-3(a) and cannot be billed as a detour; only the off-route mileage is refundable and it is the meter's own extra distance, largely the post-stop Kent Ridge/return leg.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the full charged fare of $51.00 (metered total $55.03 minus the $4.00 minimum flag-down, which is payable regardless of route) to the rider as Ryde credits, since the whole charged fare arose from a metered route the driver abandoned for an accident-blocked road; write to the driver citing RD-1 and RD-4 (the incident was on the route abandoned, not the optimal route driven). No account flag: the driver has 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days, so RD-6 does not apply.

segment_findings.reason: The single off-optimal-route segment of ~11.6 km / ~20 min min (driver drove ECP→PIE instead of the optimal ECP→KPE, trace on KPE only once at 21:41:15 and never in the 21:47:45–21:52:15 window where the trace sits ≈1 km from the KPE). The RD-4 accident (21:26, KPE towards Tampines) was on the road the driver abandoned, not on the road he used, so no reasonable cause; the chat contains no rider consent (RD-5). Counts under RD-1/RD-2/RD-4.

rejected_claims.reason: R-D4 requires the traffic incident to be on the abandoned (optimal) route; the Accident at 21:26 was on the KPE, which was the optimal route the driver did not drive. The record shows the detour began ~21:47, ~21 min after the incident and on a different road (PIE), so the 'unavoidable detour' claim is not corroborated.
The rider's denial of any agreed change is corroborated: the chat (21:33:35, 21:34:05) contains only pickup arrangements, no routing request or consent.

ruling.recommended_action: Hold adjudication and route to a human reviewer: (1) confirm which segment the rider's "Sure, go ahead" covers — the driver's named route (Kranji Expressway) or only his own GPS reroute — before computing any RD-2 mileage refund; (2) separately review the second, unexplained northbound diversion (GPS 18:40:40–18:44:40) and the two unmetered loops (≈3 min, ≈2 min) under the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct duty; (3) verify the meter breakdown, since metered distance_km 29.05 exceeds quoted route 20.566 km
ruling.escalation_reason: RD-5/G13: segment 1's coverage by the rider's 'Sure, go ahead' cannot be fixed from the record (no road-name/positioning fact tying the driven Kranji corridor to the named Kranji Expressway), and segment 2 is unexplained backtracking — so the RD-2 refund amount (metered RydeTAXI, ×$1.41/km over unexempt extra km) is undetermined and a human must fix segment 1's status before the amount and any account action are settled.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route deviation from the BKE alignment 18:40:10–18:47:40 via the Kranji/KJE corridor (peak ~1.40 km from the quoted route at 1.387,103.763), with a ~2 min loop at 1.3871,103.7628. The driver asked before deviating (18:37:30) naming Kranji Expressway and the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead' at 18:38:10 — the rider's own complaint concedes this first detour. Consent timing satisfies RD-5 (rider's message precedes the segment start), but no record ties the driven segment to Kranji Expressway (no road-name fact, no stop on it, no positioning message), so under RD-5/G13 the scope is undetermined rather than exempt. RD-4 could not exempt it (no incidents; only BKE band 5 / PIE band 4, never band 1–2).

18:46:40–18:52:40: instead of continuing, the cab turned back north-east up the BKE at 1.3904,103.7742 → 1.3923,103.7756 and ran ~7 km in the wrong direction past 1.384/1.375/1.369 to ≈1.358,103.7821 before U-turning and re-running the same stretch south. Unexplained and unconsented: the rider was never asked (his complaint is exactly this, 'he went off the route a second time without asking'); the driver's statement 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting' is a claim, not the rider's own message (G11); nothing in the chat covers it. No RD-4 exemption (no incidents; either highway's band is 4/5, so congestion on the BKE cannot justify driving the BKE the other way). It fails the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct duty; ~6 km of unexempt extra distance enters the RD-2 (RydeTAXI) refund base.

18:59:10–19:01:00 unexplained loop into/around the PIE (1.3343,103.8110 → 1.3309,103.8154 → 1.3333,103.8169, ~2 min, ~1 km back up the already-completed route) on a stretch that otherwise follows the quoted route. No rider request, no named road, no chat coverage (RD-3 / RD-1); adds unexplained distance. RD-3(c) also notes that for the non-RydeTAXI wait-fee rule such stops are unchargeable, and here the same principle applies to the distance generated by the stop.

rejected_claims.reason: G11 — the driver's own account ('the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting') is a claim, not the rider's consent; no rider message authorises the second deviation, and the rider's complaint says he was not asked. RD-4 gives no exemption (no incidents, no band 1–2 on the alternative).

Partially accepted only: the rider's 'Sure, go ahead' (18:38:10) covers a route to get to the destination, not the driver's own backtracking; the wording names Kranji Expressway and the record cannot tie the driven segment to it (RD-5/G13), so it cannot be treated as blanket consent to everything driven thereafter.
RD-4 — the only traffic facts are BKE speed band 5 and PIE band 4 windows; incidents list is empty, no band 1–2 on the replaced optimal route, rain 0. No incident-based exemption for any segment.
RD-6 requires driver.route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; profile shows 0, so no flag_account even with segment 2 counting.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$13.22 (Ryde voucher) for the unexplained off-route distance; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).

segment_findings.reason: GPS detour from the quoted East Coast Parkway route between ~22:56 and ~23:26 (Ubi Loop and a second loop east of the PIE, rejoining at ~1.330269,103.975503); extra distance ≈2.3 km metered. Not covered by RD-5 (no rider consent message; chat contains only pickup arrangements), not exempt under RD-4 (no traffic incidents; ECP/Airport Boulevard band 3 is not band 1–2 and cannot exempt alone).

rejected_claims.reason: 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' — a reroute does not itself excuse the deviation; no RD-4 traffic cause and no rider consent, so the extra distance is not exempt.
Rider asked for the full ~3 km difference back; the medallion/meter difference is 3.13 km, but only the unexplained off-route segment (≈2.3 km) is refundable, per RD-2.

ruling.recommended_action: Reject the fare-refund claim: RydeX is a fixed-quote service ($34.38 quoted at booking, unchanged after the trip) and the driven distance matches the quoted route (16.6 km both); no unpublished add-ons were charged (tolls $0, waiting $0, edit-destination $0). No further fare action; keep the trip and GPS trace on file.

segment_findings.reason: Small off-route excursion around 09:08–09:12 (max cross-track ~0.9 km, several 30 s samples looping in the lon 103.7747–103.7774 / lat ~1.290 band vs the quoted route near 1.2991,103.7800). No rider consent on record (chat is pickup-only), no traffic incident in the record for the replaced segment (traffic.incidents = []), so the driver's 'GPS rerouted me' statement does not exempt it under RD-4. Under RD-1 it is an unexplained deviation; however the trip is RydeX (fixed quote, fare.pricing='fixed') and fare is not distance-based, so RD-2's non-metered branch yields $0.00 refundable (no ERP/toll or unpublished add-on on the segment).

rejected_claims.reason: RydeX is non-metered: fare is the fixed booking quote ($34.38) and did not change with the driven distance; the driven trace matches the 16.587 km quoted route (any excursion ≲1 km, ≈3–5%), and no ERP/toll or unpublished item was charged, so the refundable amount under RD-2 is $0.00.

No traffic incident in the record (traffic.incidents = []) supporting a 'reasonable cause' reroute under RD-4; the driver's statement alone does not exempt the small deviation. This does not change the outcome because the fixed-quote fare was unaffected.

ruling.recommended_action: Reject the fare-difference claim: trip was a fixed-price RydeX booking and the off-route segment was covered by the rider's own prior chat consent; no refund or account flag.

segment_findings.reason: Driver messaged at 10:01:00, before leaving the optimal TPE route, naming a specific road ('go round via Halus Link?'), and the rider replied at 10:01:40 'Sure, go ahead' — rider's own consent timestamped before the segment start (≈10:04). The GPS trace ties the driven loop (≈1.3875,103.9230 at 10:05:20, returning via 1.3854,103.9209 at 10:06:50) to the named Halus Link/TPE interchange area, so the scope of consent covers this segment: no deviation under RD-5, and hence no unexempted segment under RD-1. (RD-4(b) not met — both speed bands read 4, incidents empty — but RD-4 is not needed given consent.)

rejected_claims.reason: RydeX is a fixed-quote, non-metered service: the fare (base 3.90 + distance 14.02 + time 3.93 + platform 1.47 = 23.32) is set at booking and does not change with mileage; no unpublished or unsupported surcharge was added, so FARE-1/FARE-2 refund the difference back. The complaint's premise ('paid more than the estimate') cannot be verified because quoted_total is null in the record; missing evidence does not favour either side.

The driver's stated justification (traffic build-up on TPE) is not an exempting cause here: incident list is empty (RD-4(a) fails) and the TPE/Punggol Road speed bands read band 4, not band 1/2 (RD-4(b) is corroborative only and does not exempt on its own). The segment is exempt solely on the rider's recorded prior consent (RD-5), not on the traffic claim.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$6.02 as a Ryde voucher (14.49 − 8.569 = 5.921 km at the trip's meter rate of $1.41/km) + flag_account for driver review under RD-6

segment_findings.reason: GPS trace (30 s thinned) leaves the quoted optimal route after ~12:11 and runs ~6 km west/south-west to ~1.292, 103.784 (12:26) before returning to NUS at 12:28:10; total 14.49 km vs quoted 8.569 km. No rider consent (chat has no message about routing), no traffic exemption (incidents empty; speed bands 4 and 5, not band 1–2), so the extra distance is unexempted under RD-1/RD-2, with RD-3 (no rider-named stop) and RD-5 (no pre-departure agreement; driver's GPS claim is not consent, G11) not applying.

rejected_claims.reason: "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me" is a claim, not rider consent (RD-5, G11); no chat message shows any agreement to an alternative route, and no LTA incident or low-speed band supports a reasonable-cause reroute (RD-4).
The rider's own rounding (9 km / 14 km) is close to but not identical to the record: quoted 8.569 km, metered 14.49 km; the refund is computed on the record values, not the rounded ones.

ruling.recommended_action: Close with no refund; send the rider an explanation that RydeTAXI fares are metered and that the GPS trace matched the app's shortest route, with the PIE delay and heavy rain noted.

segment_findings.reason: Pre-pickup approach loop around Tampines (GPS 17:14:30–17:19:30, before pickup at 17:20:00) — occurred before the passenger was on board and adds nothing to the metered trip; no charge to the rider, so it cannot be an RD-1 off-route segment.

rejected_claims.reason: The 'longer route' claim is not supported: from pickup the GPS trace tracks the quoted polyline, and total driven distance (8.81 km metered) is below the 8.877 km quoted, so nothing beyond the quoted route was charged.
Accepted as consistent with the record (PIE band 5 across the trip window and heavy rain) but not needed to exempt anything, since no detour segment exists.

ruling.recommended_action: Reject the fare-adjustment request (fixed-fare RydeX; no chargeable deviation established) and send a warning letter to driver for deviating without informing the rider; keep the account-review referral open given 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days.

segment_findings.reason: GPS samples near 14:22:50–14:23:20 sit ~0.5–1.0 km off the quoted AYE line; with 30 s sampling (~0.3 km per sample) and no per-segment fact id or extra_km, the record cannot tie this to a chargeable RD-1 off-route segment. No chat consent exists and no RD-4 incident/band evidence applies; for RydeX the finding is amount-neutral (no refundable fare item), so it does not change the ruling.

GPS samples near 14:24:20–14:25:20 run north of the AYE corridor; again the trace gives no measured extra_km and cannot be reliably separated from map-matching scatter at this sampling interval. No rider agreement on record (chat empty) and no traffic incident on the replaced segment, so this is at most an unmeasured RD-1 breach with zero monetary effect on a fixed-fare RydeX trip.

rejected_claims.reason: RydeX is a fixed-fare service: extra distance during the trip does not change the fare, so no distance-based overcharge exists to refund (RD-2 non-metered branch, FARE-1).
No meter on RydeX; the quoted and recorded distance are identical (10.761 km), and the fare line items add to the fixed total 25.04 with no meter component.

The driver's statement is a bare claim; there is no LTA traffic incident on the replaced optimal-route segment and no band 1/2 congestion record, and the chat is empty, so neither RD-4 nor RD-5 exempts any deviation.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$4.71 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexcused detour (extra metered distance), and remind the driver that a route change requires the rider's agreement before leaving the optimal route.

segment_findings.reason: Net-off-route excursion beyond the quoted route, ≈2.99 km (metered 10.87 km vs quoted 7.884 km), visible in the GPS trace from 18:19:40 onward. The driver's only route-change message (c1, 18:28:50) came nine minutes after the deviation had begun and the rider never replied, so no RD-5 consent exists; the claimed verbal 'no objection' is not consent (G11). The message names Outram Road while the driven loop runs north/north-east and is nowhere attributable to Outram Road, so even a deemed agreement cannot be tied to this segment (G13). No traffic fact covers the replaced optimal corridor (speed-band facts relate to NEW BRIDGE ROAD / SENTOSA GATEWAY, and both are band 3 and on the route actually driven), so RD-4 gives no exemption. RD-2 refund = 2.99 km × $1.41/km = $4.22 (capped by the metered fare differential of $4.23).

rejected_claims.reason: The driver claims the rider did not object to the alternative road, but his own chat message was sent at 18:28:50 — after the GPS trace shows the deviation had already begun (18:19:40) and after the taxi had already swept back past the pickup area. Under RD-5 consent must precede the detour and must be the rider's own message; a verbally claimed, post-hoc non-objection is not consent (G11).

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.71 (voucher) to the rider for the ~1.85 km detour loop to the Selatar petrol station; no other fare item is chargeable; note the RD-1 breach on the driver's record (no account flag, no prior upheld route dispute).

segment_findings.reason: Deviation into the Selatar corridor and back out. The rider consented to the driver's own named 'petrol station just ahead' as a roadside stop (RD-3(a)); a stop on the corridor is not a routing request, so the excursion is covered by RD-5.

The consolidated ~1-minute stop at 1.4007,103.8278 (21:48:30–21:49:40) matches the agreed fuel stop; the rider's 'he never stopped' assertion is not supported by the trace, and no stop-in-transit waiting fee is chargeable (RD-3(c)).

Post-stop loop away from the route and onto the wrong carriageway of the TPE (~1.85 km). Not covered by the consented stop or any general route authorisation; unexplained under RD-1, no RD-4 incident support, so extra_km enters RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider says the driver never stopped for petrol; the GPS trace shows a consolidated stationary window (~21:48:30–21:49:40) at the service-station area, consistent with a brief fuel stop.
The driver argues the rider's agreement to a 'short stop' covered the route change; RD-5 consent covers only the consented stop, not the additional ~1.85 km loop that followed it.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$6.39 via Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempt detour on the metered RydeTAXI fare; note the RD-1 violation on the driver record and send the account for review (RD-6) — waiver requires rider consent before the detour, not after. + flag_account
ruling.escalation_reason: Undetermined segment (seg2): the rider's consent scope for the ECP loop cannot be matched to the driven road (G13), the GPS is thinned to 30 s samples (no fine-grained dawn loop capture), the driver gave no account of Bedok South Ave 3, and no LTA incident record exists — any of which would change the amount or the flag.

segment_findings.reason: GPS 22:42:25–22:44:55 shows a northbound back-track off the app route (Victoria St / Lavender: 1.2803,103.8549 → 1.2783,103.8585 → 1.2803,103.8598) before re-joining at Beach Road/ECP. The rider's consent message is at 23:03:40, ~20 min after this detour began, and names Bedok South Ave 3 which cannot cover this earlier opposite-direction segment, so it cannot be exempted under RD-5; traffic.incidents is empty and the relevant bands are band 4, so RD-4 does not exempt it.

The ECP loop near Bedok North Ave 3 / Tanah Merah coincides with the driver's 23:03:00 message and the rider's 23:03:40 'Sure, go ahead'. The rider named no road and the driver named Bedok South Avenue 3, but no record ties the driven loop to that road (G13); with 30 s-thinned GPS the ordering of the message vs. the loop's start cannot be fixed. Consent scope is unreadable → undetermined (RD-5).

The remaining distance difference between the quoted route (21.553 km) and the metered trip (24.71 km) that is not attributable to the identified off-route segments is map-matching residual (<0.25 km) and is not refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver asserts the rider agreed verbally before turning off via Bedok South Avenue 3; a consent claim appearing only in the driver's statement does not constitute consent (G11), and the chat shows no pre-detour consent message.

ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to a human reviewer for the SAFE-1 driver-conduct issue (abusive chat message 'Shut up and let me drive.') and complete the route-deviation/overcharge assessment: pull the full (unthinned) GPS trace to measure the unexcused off-route segment's extra_km and compute the RD-2 partial refund at $1.41/km on this metered RydeTAXI fare, and consider an account-review referral for the driver's conduct and suspected detour."

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment from approx. 08:58 to 09:06 (GPS: 1.324903/103.885034 → looping east/later north around 1.325942/103.888892, 1.322033/103.891128 → rejoining the optimal route near the PIE). The trace departs the recorded polyline and travels 1.5–2 km off it before rejoining, adding roughly 3–5 km versus the 15.88 km optimal route (metered 20.07 km). RD-4(a) not available (no traffic incidents), RD-4(b) corroborative only, and RD-5 consent absent: the rider's only message (09:03:17) postdates the deviation and objects to it; the driver's GPS-reroute claim is untimed and, per G11, a statement is not consent. Per RD-1/RD-2 this unexcused segment supports a partial refund of extra_km × $1.41/km on this metered (RydeTAXI) trip; exact extra_km is for the reviewer because the trace is thinned.

rejected_claims.reason: Claim that 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is not supported as a lawful explanation: there is no traffic incident or road-closure record on the optimal route (RD-4(a) fails), the only speed-band entries are band 4, which cannot exempt on its own (RD-4(b)); and system GPS overrides the driver's statement. It also provides no rider consent (G11).

The driver's assertion 'Nothing wrong with the fare' is contradicted by the record: metered distance 20.07 km against a 15.88 km optimal route over a 30m35s trip, with an observable off-route loop; the route-deviation/overcharge claim is referred to the reviewer rather than dismissed.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher, and review the driver's "I'm Here" tap against GPS (button pressed while ~600 m away) for cancellation-button abuse.

rejected_claims.reason: His claim of pressing I'm Here and waiting >3 min *at the pickup* is contradicted by his own GPS trace, which shows the vehicle stationary ~600 m from the pickup point for the whole wait period; the rider's 12:06:55 message corroborates that no car was at the pickup.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the S$6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no driver account flag (driver did reach the pickup point and simply cancelled before the 3-minute wait completed).

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's statement and chat message ('Waited more than 3 min, cancelling', 14:14:40) claim >3 minutes of waiting, but the system timestamps show waiting began at the 'I'm Here' press 14:13:10 and the trip was cancelled at 14:14:50 — 100 seconds, not more than 180. System records override statements.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.44 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (RydeTAXI metered excess distance × S$1.41/km) and note the driver's RD-1 breach on file.

segment_findings.reason: Eastern loop off the AYE onto the East Coast / Marina corridor before rejoining (≈09:57:30–10:09:15), ~4.2 km extra; the driver's 10:06 message sought consent only after this segment had begun (RD-5 requires consent before the detour), it named Prince George's Park, and the trace is nowhere near there (G13); no traffic incident on this substituted path (RD-4). Not exempt.

Small northward diversion near Jurong (≈10:17–10:21, via 1.2971,103.7833 / 1.3003,103.7781) before rejoining; ~1.3 km. The rider's 10:06 consent post-dates the segment's start and no record ties this stretch to the named road Prince George's Park (RD-5/G13).
Final approach into Jurong East MRT follows the quoted polyline within the 30 s sampling / 0.2 km match noise; no material off-route distance (RD-1 data-layer tolerance).

rejected_claims.reason: The driver attributes the whole diversion to the AYE breakdown (09:47 incident exists and is on-route), but the trace shows the driver on the AYE at normal speed (35–43 km/h) from ≈10:21, and the 4.2 km eastern loop via the East Coast corridor is not explained by that single incident; RD-4 requires the incident to justify the substituted segment, and it does not.

The rider's 'Sure, go ahead.' is real but post-dates the start of the off-route driving and names Prince George's Park, a road the trace does not use; it does not cover the deviated segment (RD-5, G11/G13).

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee (driver paid $4.50); inform rider the fee stands because arrival was confirmed via platform/GPS and the wait exceeded 6 minutes.

rejected_claims.reason: Rider's own complaint places his arrival about a minute after the 17:22:30 cancellation; by then the driver had already been in-range at the pickup point for ~3:30–4:00, so the NS-1 wait condition had already been met.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and close the case; no driver account action.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and remind the driver that "I'm Here" and the waiting-fee/no-show steps require ≥ 3 min of GPS-verified waiting at the pickup point before cancellation.

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $7.77 to the rider for the un-exempt 4.38 km detour (overcharged metered distance) and note the driver's RD-1 breach; no account flag needed.

RD-1 is satisfied on the record: one off-route segment is measured, 09:24–09:30, where 3.78 km was driven against 0.71 km of optimal route, adding 3.07 km and straying up to 688 m from the route [F3]. Being unexplained by any exemption, that segment is an unexempted detour under RD-1 [F3][RD-1].

No reasonable-cause exemption is available for that segment [F3]. There is no incident record near the route in the trip window, so RD-4(a) fails [F13][RD-4]; the only traffic records are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard, well above the band 1–2 congestion definition, and a speed band cannot exempt standing alone, so RD-4(b) does not help [F11][F12][RD-4]. Weather was fair with no rain, removing any weather excuse [F14][RD-4].

No rider consent covers the segment [F3]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, and it contains only the 09:04 pickup greeting with the rider's backpack and the 09:05 driver car description — no rider message agreeing to any route, sent before the 09:24 segment started [F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a bare claim appearing only in his own statement, which under RD-5/G11 is not rider consent [F10][RD-5]. The rider also named no stop, so RD-3 gives no exemption either [F7][F8][RD-3].

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the extra distance enters the fare, and RD-2 refunds only the mileage unit of the unexempted segment [F6][RD-2]. The rate is this trip's own distance fare divided by distance driven: $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.41008.../km, as the trace states it — never rounded [F6][RD-2]. The refund is therefore 3.07 km × $1.41008.../km = $4.33 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The gap between the segment's 3.07 km and the 3.20 km excess-distance line (and the +3.2 km total) is corridor/map-matching mileage not attributable to any segment and is not refundable [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]. Time and waiting components add nothing: waiting was $0.00 and no waiting-fee condition was triggered, so no fee-waived issue arises [F6][NS-6].

The RD-6 account flag precondition is not met: the driver's 90-day profile shows 0 route disputes upheld, so this single first-time segment cannot make the breach "repeated" and no flag_account attaches [F16][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read every message, the complaint and the driver's statement. The chat is a pickup greeting and a car description; the complaint is a fare/routing complaint; the statement is a bare explanation of the route. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10]. The record settles every element this ruling needs — a measured off-route segment, the fare rate and the absence of any consent message — so the evidence is sufficient [F3][F6][F9].

ruling.reasoning:
Service type is RydeTAXI, so the trip is metered: extra distance directly inflates the fare (policy §0, RD-2). Rider complaint = driver left the quoted route silently; driver says "GPS rerouted" — no traffic justification is on the record (traffic.incidents = [], speed bands on the route are band 5, i.e. free flow, so RD-4 gives no exemption). Chat contains only a pickup arrangement (black backpack / blue Prius) — nothing before the deviation, so RD-5 consent does not exist; the driver's claim of GPS rerouting is not rider consent.

Route reconstruction: the driver followed the quoted polyline from Raffles Place through the ECP corridor (matches polyline points up to ~1.2960,103.8950). A first divergence appears between the 09:24:00 sample (1.30809,103.93088) and 09:24:30 (1.309079,103.933754), where the driver passed south of and then north of the ECP alignment around 1.3102–1.3112,103.9340–103.9350 (quoted route runs 1.3093,103.93514 → 1.31044,103.93924). The GPS then runs off the line for ~11 minutes: 09:25:00 1.311484,103.934355; 09:25:30 1.314159,103.934176; 09:26:00 1.315803,103.935313; 09:26:30 1.314501,103.936773; roughly 1–2.5 km west of the quoted corridor, returning to the quoted line at ~09:31:00–09:31:30 (1.311826,103.94526 / 1.31189,103.94831 vs route 1.31133,103.94231 / 1.31182,103.94498). The deviation is therefore an out-and-back loop west of the quoted route.

Length of the unexempt segment: the driven path along those GPS points is ~6.6 km, while the quoted route between the same endpoints (approx. 1.3095,103.9352 → 1.3119,103.9449) is ~1.12 km straight / ~1.3 km by road. Using the fare record's excess (fare.distance_km 24.41 − route 21.21 = 3.20 km extra) and subtracting ~0.9 km attributable to the 200 m corridor/map-matching jitter and the ramp re-join at 1.31236,103.95178, the unexempt segment contributes ~2.30 km of extra distance.

Amount: RydeTAXI distance rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = 34.42 ÷ 24.41 = SGD 1.4101/km. Refund = 2.30 × 1.4101 = SGD 3.24 (rounded to the cent). Only mileage is refunded; waiting time is not in dispute and nothing else was added (tolls 0, no add-ons), so the rest of the metered fare stands. No RD-3 rider-named stop exists (the record shows no stop the rider asked for), and RD-6 is not met (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so no account flag. No safety content anywhere in the chat, complaint or driver statement; evidence (GPS + quote + fare record) is sufficient, the thinned-but-continuous trace covers the whole trip.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$0.92 (Ryde voucher) for the unexempted 0.65 km detour via Sims Avenue/generic turn-off; note the RD-1 breach.
ruling.reasoning:
Service type RydeTAXI → metered, so extra distance directly enters the fare (RD-2). Quoted route 15.472 km / 21.8 min vs metered 19.4 km / 31.75 min; per-km rate = distance_fare ÷ distance_km = 27.35 ÷ 19.4 = 1.4098 S$/km.

Trace vs quoted route: from pickup (12:14:20) the car follows the quoted corridor along the CTE up to ~12:25:50 (1.32431,103.872327). The only off-route place is the 12:26:20–12:30:20 stretch: the car turns off at Jalan Eunos (1.32245,103.873718), stops (speed 0) at 12:26:50 on Sims Avenue East (1.32171,103.87427), then doubles back west via 1.318841,103.875336 and 1.31776,103.875035 and rejoins the corridor at ~12:30:50 (1.314746,103.874873). Off-corridor length ≈ 0.90 km, on-corridor overlap ≈ 1.30 km → net excess ≈ 0.65 km.

The chat shows the rider consented before the turn-off (12:27:30 rider "Sure, go ahead." vs turn-off at ~12:26:20–12:26:50 and stop at 12:26:50; the driver's 12:26:50 message precedes). But the consent is to a named road, Sims Avenue: under RD-5, a named-road consent covers driving on that road only and the record must tie the driven segment to that road; the SIMS AVE EAST stop over the 200 m corridor (m_from_route > 200 for 12:26:50–12:28:20) is exempt, while the post-stop westward backtrack to rejoin is not tied to Sims Avenue and is even partly under the PIE (band 2 = moderate, not the band 1–2 severe-congestion requirement) → counts (RD-4(b) cannot exempt alone).

Amount: 0.65 km × 1.4098 = S$0.92 (rounded). The metered waiting component ($0.11 = 26¢ per 45 s unit, wait standing during the Sims stop) is retained per RD-3(c) (RydeTAXI waiting is chargeable), so no separate waiver. The rider's expectation of fixed-quote pricing does not apply to RydeTAXI (policy §0).

The rider's 12:27:30 consent to 'via Sims Avenue' is a named-road consent: the stop over Sims Ave East is covered, but the backtrack to rejoin is not tied to Sims Avenue (RD-5, G13). PIE band 2 at 12:20:50 is at a different time/base point and is only corroborative, cannot alone exempt (RD-4(b), G3). Net excess ≈ 0.65 km.

The rider's own message 'Sure, go ahead.' at 12:27:30, sent before the car's own movement into the stop, consents to the driver's proposed route via Sims Avenue (RD-5). The stop at 1.32171,103.87427 (12:26:50) lies on Sims Avenue East (m_from_route > 200 m, the only 'off-route' sample) and is covered by the named-road consent (RD-3(a)/RD-5), and its standing time is chargeable on RydeTAXI (RD-3(c)); the exit from the stop back to Sims Avenue East is on Sims Avenue (RD-5).

ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat contains only a routing arrangement and the driver statement a matching account — no threat, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Route facts computed from the record: quoted route 8.432 km / 13.8 min; metered fare 10.6 km / 18.58 min; driver's GPS ends 14:40:00 at the NUS dropoff (system record). By my reconstruction the driver ran roughly 12.8 km, i.e. some 4.4 km beyond the 8.432 km.

The chat is the problem. The driver's detour proposal ("Jam on Ayer Rajah Expressway … can I go round via Clementi Road?") is timestamped 14:30:55, but the record shows the driver already heading east/south away from the quoted Jurong Town Hall Rd corridor from about 14:24–14:25 (GPS: 14:24:25 at 1.320913,103.754714; 14:25:25 at 1.316603,103.758517; then the slow 15 km/h stretch at 14:26–14:29 arcing east to ~1.3092,103.7611). The rider's reply is 14:31:35. So on the record the first clearly off-corridor movement begins before any consent existed, and even after the reply the GPS runs *north* on AYE (14:31:25 → 14:37:25, reaching 1.295862,103.785068) before a U-turn and return south down Clementi Rd / West Coast to the dropoff — i.e. for several minutes after consent the car was not on a route to NUS at all (the later 14:37:55–14:39:55 points coincide with the inbound Clementi Rd corridor near NUS).

Applying RD-5: consent must be the rider's own message sent before the detour began; a general "Sure, no problem" to a named-road proposal grants at most a designated-route authorisation, which covers driving on that named road, not the driver's own U-turn and not segments driven before the message. The driver's statement ("the rider said sure") gives no timing and cannot by itself establish prior verbal consent (G11). Because the precise detour segmentation (thin GPS, gaps at 14:24:25–14:24:55, 14:26:55–14:27:25, 14:29:55–14:30:25 and 14:31:25–14:31:55; no `gps-detour-*` ids supplied) cannot be tied reliably to the chat, and because the route-driven-vs-Clementi-Road correspondence is not directly evidenced (no road-name facts, 300 m match radius exceeded on part of the trace), the record does not settle the segment findings and the resulting amount (G12, G13). RD-4 gives no exemption: no LTA incident on the abandoned optimal route; the AYE band 2 entry lies on the *actual* AYE segment after the turn, not on the replaced optimal route, and a band alone does not exempt (RD-4(b), G3).

Consequential items: waiting_fee $0.11 is a metered wait component (RD-3(c)), not the $5 fee, so it stands; no ERP/tolls in the record, so FARE-2 not triggered; the rider was not overcharged on the base metered structure beyond the detour question. Escalation rather than a refund is required because the amount turns entirely on undetermined segment mapping; remaining over-consent kilometres ≈3.9 km ≈ $5.50 (3.9 × $1.41/km) is indicative only. The driver also never declared the amended route as a destination change (no edit-destination fee), which is relevant to metered-fare review; his 90-day route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and the profile cannot alone decide the case, so no flag is set pending human review.
ruling.escalation_reason: Off-route segmentation and the mapping of the driven segments to the chat message are undetermined (thin GPS, gaps, no road-name facts), and the finding controls both the RD-2 refund amount and any RD-6 account flag (G12, G13).

segment_findings.reason: First clear off-corridor movement (east/south from the Ayer Rajah/Jurong Town Hall corridor, GPS 14:24:25 → 14:25:25) precedes the driver's 14:30:55 chat message and the rider's 14:31:35 reply, so no RD-5 consent existed before it. The thin trace (gaps 14:24:25–14:24:55, 14:26:55–14:27:25, 14:29:55–14:30:25) makes exact segmentation unreliable, so this segment is undetermined rather than counted (G12).

Northbound AYE travel from ~14:31 (GPS 14:31:25 → 14:32:25) follows the rider's 14:31:35 reply to the driver's 14:30:55 proposal namely 'go round via Clementi Road'; a designated-route authorisation covers travel on the named road, so this portion is exempt under RD-5.

After consent the car continued north on AYE to ~1.2959,103.7851 (GPS 14:37:25) then U-turned and came back south via Clementi Rd/West Coast to the dropoff — a direction that goes nowhere near NUS at the start. Profiles: driver route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's precondition ("repeated") is not met and no account flag is raised — but the record of the RD-1 breach stands.

Northbound loop beyond AYE with the 3-minute stop (≈10:11:20–10:12:50, ≈3.4 km extra, incl. the 10:09:50–10:12:50 stop): no pre-departure consent message, no rider-named place, and the driver's own account names Clementi Ave 2, not this road; unexempted under RD-1 / RD-3 / RD-5, so its extra_km enters the RD-2 refund.

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4 requires an incident on the substituted optimal stretch listed at or before the segment start: the AYE vehicle breakdown (1.32198,103.75139, reported 09:47) is past the rejoin point (1.30679,103.76711) and does not evidence the segment actually replaced; the AYE speed band 2 is corroboration only under RD-4(b) and cannot exempt alone.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; note that the driver's "I'm Here" tap at 12:06:15 was ~780 m from Bugis Junction, so NS-1 is not satisfied; issue a driver-side reminder on the "I'm Here" button.
ruling.reasoning:
Dispute is a no-show cancellation fee (NS-0, cancelled_by = driver, driver asserts rider no-show → NS-1/NS-2). Safety screen: chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation — nothing to escalate.

NS-1 requires all three: (i) driver pressed "I'm Here"; (ii) at that moment GPS placed him at the pickup point (≤200 m); (iii) he then waited continuously >3 min within 200 m until cancelling.

(i) satisfied: driver_pressed_here_at = 12:06:15, and the driver's own chat message at 12:06:20 confirms it.

(ii) fails. Pickup (Bugis Junction) is at 1.2994, 103.8555. At 12:06:15 the GPS trace (5 s grid, thinned) puts the driver at ~1.30476, 103.85487 — roughly 0.0070° north, i.e. ≈ 780 m from the pickup point, far outside the 200 m data-layer radius. The trace from 12:06:00 through 12:09:25 shows the vehicle stationary at that same spot (speed 0–2 km/h), never approaching Bugis Junction; the last moving sample at 12:05:30 was still ~1.13 km north. The rider's message at 12:07:15 ("no car here") and the driver's stationary position agree with the rider's account; the system trace therefore overrides the driver's statement that he was at the pickup.

(iii) also fails in substance: even if the ~3 min 10 s stationary period counted, it occurred at a location ~780 m from the pickup point, not within 200 m of it.

Because NS-1 (ii) (and effectively (iii)) is not met, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full (refund_full). No flag_account: NS-2's account flag attaches only when the driver was outside the radius at the tap AND NS-1 is otherwise argued as a no-show abuse; here the fee was refunded rather than the driver's tap being used to trigger a waiting/no-show charge, and profile facts (a prior upheld no-show dispute) cannot alone justify a flag.

rejected_claims.reason: Claim that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the GPS trace: from 12:06:00 to 12:09:25 he was stationary at ~1.30476, 103.85487, about 780 m from Bugis Junction, never entering the 200 m arrival radius. System records override statements.
Driver's chat "I'm here already" at 12:06:20 is not supported by GPS: the vehicle was ~780 m north of the pickup point at that time.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat (driver's two polite messages about arrival and cancelling) and the rider's complaint contain no threat, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation — safety_concern = none.

The fee at issue is the $6.61 cancellation fee, charged on a driver-cancelled trip (cancelled_by = driver), so NS-0 routes it to NS-1/NS-2.

NS-1 (i): the record shows driver_pressed_here_at = 14:14:10, so the "I'm Here" condition is met (arrival_confirmed_by is null, so the record does not say whether it was a driver tap or platform auto — I do not attribute it beyond what the record states).

NS-1 (ii): at the moment of the tap the GPS puts the driver at 1.325166, 103.929853. The pickup (Bedok Mall) is 1.3249, 103.9296. That is ~30 m away (≈0.00027° lat ≈ 30 m; ≈0.00025° lon ≈ 28 m), well within the 200 m radius. Condition (ii) is met.

NS-1 (iii): the tap was at 14:14:10 and the cancellation at 14:15:50, i.e. exactly 1 min 40 s (100 s) later. Required is continuous waiting > 3 minutes (≥ 3:01). The GPS trace confirms this: stationary samples at 14:14:00, 14:14:30, 14:15:00 and 14:15:30, sampling interval 30 s (thinned from a 5 s grid), so the trace does cover the interval to the cancellation and shows no gap; the driver remained within ~30 m of the pickup the whole time. Less than 3 minutes elapsed.

Because condition (iii) fails, NS-1 is not satisfied → NS-2: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider (refund_full, $6.61). No flag_account is warranted: NS-2's flag attaches only when the "I'm Here" tap was made while GPS showed the driver NOT at the pickup, which is not the case here (he was ~30 m away), and the driver's no-show profile count (no_show_disputes_upheld_90d = 1) is a profile fact that cannot decide this case or trigger a flag on its own.

The driver's statement ("waited for the rider, then cancelled as a no-show") and his chat claim "3 min up" conflict with the timestamps: the system records (timeline and GPS) override statements, and the elapsed wait was 100 s. The rider's own words ("barely two minutes") match the record.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that he waited the full no-show period (and the chat message '3 min up') is contradicted by the system record: driver_pressed_here_at 14:14:10 -> cancelled_at 14:15:50 is only 100 seconds, and the GPS samples at 14:14:00–14:15:30 show him stationary at the pickup throughout. NS-1(iii) requires > 3 minutes of continuous waiting, which is not met.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$7.90 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (5.60 extra km on the un-exempt segment x S$1.41/km metered rate), and send the driver's account to Ryde review as a repeated route-deviation breach + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
Service type is RydeTAXI, so the fare is metered and detour kilometres feed directly into the fare; the overcharge is measured per RD-2 as extra_km x per-km rate.

Measured detour (GPS, 30 s thinned grid). The quoted route (10.993 km) runs from NEX Serangoon south along Upper Serangoon / Bendemeer / Kallang to Suntec. The executed trace follows it to about 1.3427,103.8687, then turns NE into Braddell Road (1.3437,103.86696 -> 1.34428,103.86471 -> 1.34354,103.8625 -> 1.34276,103.86093), reaches 1.34054,103.8617 at 22:45:55, doubles back about 143 m SE and re-joins the corridor at 1.3383,103.8623. That loop adds roughly 0.6-0.7 km - within GPS matching noise (0.2 km) plus a short jog, not a deviation. The real problem starts at 22:47:55 (1.33157,103.86256, still on the corridor): the trace turns SE down Paya Lebar Road (1.33013,103.86378 -> 1.32916,103.86592 -> 1.32838,103.86813 -> 1.32727,103.86981 -> 1.32557,103.87143 -> 1.32377,103.87293, 0 km/h at 22:51:25), then E along the PIE (1.32163,103.87456 -> 1.31992,103.87505), down to 1.31667,103.87511 (8.1 km/h), NE to 1.31680,103.87797, SE to 1.31448,103.87931 and 1.31317,103.8821, out to the furthest point 1.31115,103.88538 at 22:58:55, then back W via 1.31067,103.88309 -> 1.31031,103.88138 -> 1.30989,103.87942, with a 134 m W jog at 23:01:25, re-joining the corridor at about 23:04 (1.299,103.8776). Traced length of that stretch is about 11.9 km against about 1.8 km for the corridor sub-segment (1.33157,103.86256)-(1.299,103.8776), i.e. about 10 km of extra driving over a stretch the quoted route covers in about 1.7 km. It is one continuous, deliberate detour, so RD-1 treats it as a single un-exempt segment (seg1).

No exemption applies. Traffic: there is no LTA incident (incidents = []), so RD-4(a) fails; the only band-2 record on a route road is PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY SYN-0009 (22:32:55-22:54:50), which is band 2 on the PIE the driver said he was avoiding, and under RD-4(b) a speed band alone is only corroborative in the MVP and cannot exempt; the driven Paya Lebar Road / eastern-PIE stretch has no band 1-2 record. Consent (RD-5): the only chat is the driver at 22:51:15 ("traffic on Pan Island Expressway is building up, mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?") and the rider at 22:51:55 ("Sure, go ahead."). (i) The rider's agreement covers only Guillemard Road, and the record affirmatively places the driven segment elsewhere: the driver's own statement routes him via Guillemard Road while every halfway-consistent GPS point at that time is on Paya Lebar Road / the eastern PIE, and nothing shows the car on Guillemard Road, so the named-road agreement does not cover seg1 - this is a finding of "counts", not "undetermined", because the record contradicts rather than fails to tie the segment. (ii) In any event the consent (22:51:55) postdates the off-route movement (begun about 22:47:55, the car already at 1.33013,103.86378 by 22:48:25), so it is not consent "before you go". (iii) The 22:46:25 mid-segment halt (movement 30 m in 30 s) was a brief stop, and a stop the rider asked for without naming a place does not excuse the driver's far-flung choice of route (RD-3); in any case it occurred before the 22:47:55 deviation. The driver's claim of verbal agreement beyond the record is a claim only (G11). Waiting fee of 0.11 is a metered taxi minute, not the $5 boarding wait.

Amount (RD-2, RydeTAXI). Metered rate = distance_fare 19.15 / distance_km 13.58 = S$1.41/km. The traced excess (roughly 10 km) and the corridor-ratio estimate (route 10.993 km at a 41% straight-line ratio over the 6.525 km straight pickup-to-dropoff, so about 2.95 km corridor over that stretch -> about 8.9 km extra) bracket the excess at roughly 9-10 km, but the 30 s thinning can smooth the loop, so I hold only part of that differential: 5.60 extra km x S$1.41 = S$7.90. The rider still pays the metered waiting component and the unexplained remainder of the 2.587 km distance difference (13.58 vs 10.993 km), which is not recoverable under RD-2.

Flag. This is an upheld deviation with a refund > 0, and the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2, so RD-6 applies and the case is flagged for account review as repeated. Safety screen: the chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, abuse, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; no safety escalation.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route from about 22:47:55 (1.33157,103.86256) until re-joining the quoted corridor at about 23:04 (1.299,103.8776): SE down Paya Lebar Road, E along the PIE to the furthest point 1.31115,103.88538 (22:58:55), then back W to the corridor. Extra about 10 km (driven about 11.9 km vs quoted about 1.8 km between the same endpoints). Un-exempt: no LTA incident, so RD-4(a) fails; the band-2 record SYN-0009 is on the PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY the detour was meant to avoid and is only corroborative under RD-4(b); and the 22:51:15 driver message plus the 22:51:55 rider agreement name Guillemard Road, which the record affirmatively places elsewhere (the driver's own statement routes him via Guillemard Road while every halfway-consistent GPS point sits on Paya Lebar Road / the eastern PIE; none on Guillemard, Upper Serangoon, Bendemeer or Kallang), so the named-road agreement does not cover this segment and the consent in any event postdates the off-route movement by over four minutes (RD-5). RD-1 un-exempt segment; refunded per RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: RD-5/G11: a driver's claim that the rider agreed verbally beyond the record is not consent; only the rider's own pre-detour message counts. The only recorded rider message is the 22:51:55 'Sure, go ahead.', which postdates the about-22:47:55 off-route movement and covers a road the record does not tie to the driven path.

RD-4(b): the band-2 record is on PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY SYN-0009; a speed band alone, on a road that was only the alternative, does not exempt the detour in the MVP, and there is no LTA incident (RD-4(a) unmet).

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee; no refund due. Note rider's claim that she arrived "a minute after cancellation" is consistent with the driver having lawfully waited out the 3 minutes before cancelling.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat contains only the driver's arrival notice and his cancellation notice; the complaint is a fee grievance. No threat, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation.

No-show analysis under NS-0 → NS-1: cancellation was by the driver on a contended rider no-show, and no-show threshold is not given in the record, so the default (iii) of >3 minutes applies (the record's free_wait_time is not a no-show threshold; NS-1). (i) Arrival was confirmed by driver tap: trip.driver_pressed_here_at = 17:19:15, matching chat message 17:19:25 "I'm here at the pickup point". (ii) At that tap the GPS fix (17:19:00, thinned 30 s grid) reads lat 1.283934, lon 103.850939, which is ~70 m from the pickup point (1.2840, 103.8513) — well within the 200 m data-layer radius, and the next two fixes (17:19:30, 17:20:00, 17:20:30, 17:21:00, 17:21:30, 17:22:00, 17:22:30, 17:22:55) stay stationary at ~1.28391–1.28394, 103.850941–103.850959, i.e. continuously inside the radius. (iii) Continuous wait from the 17:19:15 tap to the 17:22:55 cancellation = 3 min 40 s, exceeding the >3 min (≥3:01) requirement. The trace is continuous on the 30 s grid with no gap (largest gap 25 s), so NS-1's anti-gap proviso (G12) is not triggered. All three NS-1 elements are satisfied → the $6.61 rider cancellation fee stands, $4.50 of it to the driver, and the ruling is no_action with no amount.

Rider's complaint ("I came out a minute after the driver cancelled") does not defeat the fee: the fee is earned by the driver completing a lawful 3-minute wait, not by the rider's absence at that instant; NS-4's 3-minute grace period applies only to rider-initiated cancellations, and NS-8 (driver-late free cancellation) is not Ryde policy and there is no ETA field in any event.

No driver-side flag: the arrival tap took place within the 200 m pickup radius, so NS-2's fraudulent-tap flag condition is not met, and RD-6 is inapplicable (no route deviation of any kind — all fixes lie on the pickup approach corridor).

rejected_claims.reason: Rider says she came out a minute after the driver cancelled, so she should not be charged. The GPS trace shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 17:19:15 inside the 200 m pickup radius and remained stationary there continuously until cancelling at 17:22:55 (3 min 40 s), satisfying NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii); the $6.61 fee is valid and NS-4's 3-minute grace period does not apply to a driver-initiated no-show cancellation.

Driver's statement that he 'waited over 3 minutes' is not taken on his word: it is independently corroborated by the GPS trace (stationary within the pickup radius from 17:19:00 to 17:22:55) and by his 17:22:45 cancellation message.

ruling.recommended_action: Reverse the $6.61 cancellation fee and issue the rider a $6.61 Ryde voucher (fee was charged although the rider cancelled within the 3-minute free window); no driver-side action.
ruling.reasoning:
Service type is RydeX (non-metered, fixed quote), so the only disputed item is the $6.61 cancellation fee. cancelled_by = rider, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4 (on-demand ride, rider cancellation).

Timing (system records, which override statements): requested_at 18:22:30, accepted_at 18:23:00, cancelled_at 18:25:30 → elapsed since matching = exactly 2 min 30 s, i.e. ≤ 3:00. Under NS-4, cancellations within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable; the rider's claim that she cancelled under 3 minutes is corroborated by the timeline. Despite this, fare.cancellation_fee = 6.61 was charged → full refund of $6.61 (refund_full).

NS-1/NS-2 (driver-side no-show) are not engaged: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at = null, driver_arrived_at = null, arrival_confirmed_by = null), and the cancellation was by the rider, not the driver. NS-6 (waiting fee) does not apply — no $5.00 waiting fee was charged and the trip was never completed. The rider was in fact never picked up: no pickup_at and no completed leg appear in the timeline, only the driver approaching (GPS ends ~1.6 km from Jurong East MRT at 18:25:30). The driver's ETA of "5 min more" and the fair-weather/traffic-band-4 record are consistent with the driver still being en route, which is why a fee should not have been applied. The 30-day dispute window (NS-7) is satisfied (trip 2026-09-15, dispute filed same day), and the refund is issued as a voucher.

Safety screening (SAFE-1/SAFE-2): chat is two neutral messages ("How long will you be?", "5 min more, traffic is slow"); no threats, harassment, sexual remarks, dangerous-driving or injury allegation anywhere in the complaint or driver statement → no safety escalation.

Profile facts (driver disputes_90d = 0, no prior upheld route/no-show disputes) are noted for context only and do not affect the outcome; no grounds for RD-6 or NS-2 account flagging.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver says only that he was on his way when the rider cancelled; the system timeline (cancelled_by = rider at 18:25:30, 2 min 30 s after matching) shows the rider was never picked up and that no no-show fee basis exists under NS-1 (driver never pressed 'I'm Here', never within 200 m of pickup).

Rider's assertion that the driver 'was nowhere near' is directionally corroborated by GPS (driver still ~1.6 km from pickup at cancellation), but it is not needed for the outcome: the fee fails solely on the 3-minute NS-4 window. Stated only as context, not as a basis for the refund amount.

ruling.recommended_action: Explain to the rider that $6.61 applies because the cancellation came 3 min 20 s after matching; note Ryde has no "driver late vs ETA" free-cancellation rule. No refund due.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat is a two-message ETA exchange ("How long will you be?" / "About 5 min, traffic"), the rider's complaint is a fare objection, and the driver's statement ("I was on my way when the rider cancelled") contains no threat, abuse, harassment, sexual remark, or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Classification: cancelled_by = rider, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4 (immediate booking, no scheduled-time field). Matching at 21:30:00, cancelled at 21:33:20 → elapsed 200 s = 3 min 20 s, which is beyond the 3-minute grace window. NS-4: cancellations made more than 3 minutes after matching → the $6.61 cancellation fee stands; cancellations within 3:00 are not chargeable, so the rider misses the free window by 20 seconds. Ryde publishes no "driver later than ETA → free cancellation" rule (NS-8, informational only, not citable), and NS-4 expressly says the driver's not having arrived is not a ground for free cancellation; the rider's remedy is a discretionary human appeal under NS-7.

The driver-side no-show mechanism (NS-1/NS-2) is not engaged: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at = null), no arrival was confirmed, and the trip was cancelled by the rider, so there is nothing to refund under those clauses. The rider's "driver was still far away" claim is supported by the GPS trace (at 21:33:20 the driver was still ~4 km from the NUS pickup on Pasir Panjang, and the incident-free band 6 speed record corroborates slow going), but it is legally irrelevant under NS-4 for this service/fare type.

Rider profile shows disputes_90d = 0; the driver's single prior upheld no-show dispute does not trigger RD-6 (no route-deviation finding here, no refund > 0), so no account flag.

Evidence status: sufficient — the timeline is complete (match, cancellation time, cancelling party) and the GPS trace covers the whole window on a 30 s grid with no gap; the only missing items (arrival taps, waiting-fee basis) are irrelevant because the rider cancelled before any arrival confirmation. Amount: null, the $6.61 stays as charged.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver was indeed still en route (GPS at 21:33:20 ≈ 4 km from pickup), but Ryde has no rule granting free cancellation because the driver is beyond the ETA (NS-8 is informational and not citable), and NS-4 does not treat the driver's absence as a ground to waive the fee.
The driver did not press 'I'm Here' and no arrival was confirmed, but NS-1/NS-2 apply to a driver-initiated no-show cancellation; here cancelled_by = rider, so that branch is not engaged.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; remind the driver that the "I'm Here" tap and an in-radius continuous 3-minute wait are mandatory before a no-show cancellation, and that unrecorded presence cannot support the fee.
ruling.reasoning: Route NS-0: cancelled_by = driver and the driver asserts rider no-show, so the case is decided under NS-1/NS-2. Non-taxi (RydeX), so no metered issues arise; the only disputed item is the $6.61 cancellation fee. NS-1 requires (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here" (or platform auto-confirmed arrival) AND (ii) at that moment GPS showed him at the pickup (≤200 m) AND (iii) continuous in-radius waiting >3 min after the tap. The record shows driver_pressed_here_at = null, arrival_confirmed_by = null, wait_started_at = null, fee_applied_at = null; the driver himself admits "I forgot to press the I'm Here button." Element (i) therefore fails, which alone is decisive under NS-2. For completeness: his vehicle (GPS at 1.43603, 103.78614 from 22:43:00 to 22:46:50) is ~230–240 m from the stated pickup point (1.436, 103.7865), i.e. outside the 200 m arrival radius used for element (ii), and the closest approach during his loop (1.43436,103.78600 at 22:41:30) is ~60 m from a different point of the polyline — not the named pickup. Also, the GPS trace is thinned (5 s grid → every 6th sample, 30 s spacing), so it cannot corroborate any "I'm Here" event; it neither fills nor creates the missing claim. Timeline check: accepted 22:37:00, driver_arrived_at 22:41:30, cancelled 22:46:50 — 9 min 50 s after acceptance, of which only the final 3 min 50 s was stationary near the pickup, but no legal start-of-wait marker exists. Since NS-1 (i) (and (ii)) are not met, the $6.61 cancellation fee did not validly arise → full refund of $6.61 (voucher form, NS-7). No RD/flag conditions: no route deviation, and route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 rules out RD-6; the driver's failure is a button/timing issue, not usage of the button with false GPS (he never used it at all), so NS-2's fraud add-on is not triggered. Safety screen: chat contains only a plain pickup identification and a wait/cancel notice; nothing threatening, abusive, sexual or dangerous — safety_concern = none.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver claims he waited 4 minutes at the pickup, but he concedes he never pressed "I'm Here" and the record has driver_pressed_here_at = null with no platform auto-confirmation. NS-1(i) therefore fails, and at the times he was stationary (22:43:00–22:46:50, 1.43603/103.78614) GPS places him ~230–240 m from the pickup point — outside the 200 m arrival radius for NS-1(ii). Unrecorded presence does not satisfy the no-show conditions.

The rider's factual account (driver cancelled, $6.61 charged) is accepted; his reason for the refund differs from the clause actually applied (NS-1/NS-2 failure, not his being en route), so the rider's justification is not relied on but the outcome is.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7), and feed the driver's "I'm Here" press at 08:47:20 — made ~740 m from the pickup point — into Ryde's abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-button review (+ flag_account).
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0: cancelled_by = driver and the driver claims rider no-show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern.

NS-1 (i): the driver pressed "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 (tl-here). (ii) Fails. The GPS at 08:47:20 (nearest sample 08:47:30) shows the car at 1.406875, 103.898794. The pickup is Punggol Waterway Point at 1.40561, 103.90168. Difference: dlat = 0.001265° = 140.7 m; dlon = 0.002886° × cos(1.406°) ≈ 0.002886 × 111,320 × 0.99970 ≈ 321.2 m. Distance = √(140.7² + 321.2²) ≈ 350.6 m. The car sat stationary at that same point from 08:47:30 through 08:51:00 (all samples 1.4068x, 103.8988), so it was ~350 m from the pickup point at the moment of the tap — far outside the 200 m arrival radius. (iii) also fails in the sense that any waiting happened at the wrong place: the rider's 08:48:20 message ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here") is consistent with the driver never being at the pickup.

NS-2: since (ii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee is refunded in full → refund_full of $6.61. Additionally, because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him >200 m from the pickup point, the clause calls for flag_account (abuse of the cancellation/waiting button). The rider's account shows no_show_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this is the driver's first flag here; the flag rests on NS-2's GPS criterion, not on the profile.

Driver statement ("waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup") is contradicted by the GPS trace, which is the overriding system record. No route-deviation issue arises: the trip was cancelled before pickup, so there is no off-route segment to assess (no gps-detour facts, fare distance_km = 0).

Safety screen: chat is a routine pickup exchange ("come out please", "where are you?", "cancelling"); no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation → safety_concern none. Evidence is sufficient (complete GPS at 30 s grid covering the whole window, timestamps on all chat messages).

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's claim to have waited at the pickup is contradicted by the GPS trace: from 08:47:30 to 08:51:00 the car was stationary at 1.4069, 103.8988, ~350 m from the pickup point at Punggol Waterway Point (1.4056, 103.9017). System records (GPS) override statements.
The 'I'm Here' tap at 08:47:20 fails NS-1(ii): GPS at that moment places the driver ~350 m from the pickup, exceeding the 200 m arrival radius.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher within 30 days; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning: Rider-side cancellation on an on-demand RydeX trip, so NS-0 routes to NS-4. Timing: accepted_at 14:05:00 → cancelled_at 14:07:55 = 2 min 55 s, i.e. within the 3-minute free-cancellation window (NS-4: "All cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable"). The $6.61 cancellation fee therefore does not stand and must be refunded in full. The driver had not arrived and was still ~2 km away at cancellation (GPS 14:05:00 at 1.32093,103.82274, heading away from the Orchard Road pickup, last sample 14:07:55 at 1.31853,103.82569), which is consistent with the rider's account, though NS-4 does not require driver delay for the waiver. The driver's cancellation/no-show branch (NS-1/NS-2) does not apply: cancelled_by = rider and the driver never pressed "I'm Here" and made no no-show claim; his statement only says he was en route. This is inside the 200 m data-layer radius, but only marginally, and the complaint is precisely that the driver was "not at the entrance where the pin was" — he admits "a short walk from the entrance." On a strict reading (ii) is satisfied only in a technical sense, while the rider's account and the driver's own statement are consistent that he was not at the pin. The more robust ground for the rider is NS-1(iii).

NS-1(iii): from 14:06:15 to 14:09:55 is 3 min 40 s (220 s > 180 s), so the continuous-wait requirement is met on the timeline. However, the policy requires continuous waiting *at the pickup point*: tl-here's within_200m_after_tap_s. The GPS samples during the wait (14:06–14:09) are all clustered at ~1.29184, 103.84753 — the same ~180 m offset position, not the pin. The record cannot establish that the driver waited within the pickup radius/at the entrance as opposed to remaining parked where he was when he tapped; his own statement confirms the latter ("parked at the pickup, a short walk from the entrance"). The rider was at the entrance and contacted him at 14:07:55 ("I'm at the entrance, I don't see you"); the driver neither moved toward the pin nor clarified the meeting point — he went straight to cancellation.

Conclusion: the driver's claim of a valid rider no-show is not established to the NS-1 standard (location element (ii)/(iii) not reliably satisfied), so NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full, refund_full $6.61 (voucher per NS-7). NS-2's extra flag_account is not triggered because m_from_pickup_at_tap (≈181 m) is not > 200 m, so no fraud flag on the arrival tap. Driver profile is not used to decide the case.

Serialisation caveat for reviewers: these coordinates are ~1.5–2 km off the recorded pickup/dropoff points; comparisons above are made internally between the pin, route and GPS trace as recorded, which are mutually consistent, and the margin at 181 m is small, so a human may wish to re-verify the tap position before treating the tap as compliant.
